families.anatomy:
The bootstrap-start family has TWO physically distinct response shapes, gated on whether `route` was supplied:

1) ROUTE-MENU (`workflow:bootstrap:start::route-menu`, 265 rows, p50≈3.3KB, max 9.6KB). Top keys: `kind`, `intent`, `projectId`, `routeOptions[]`, `message`. `routeOptions[]` (p50 2337B, max 7217B) is the structured decision surface: each option carries `route`, `why`, and for recipes `recipeSlug`/`fit`/`fitMissing`/`retrievalScore`/`collisions` plus — only on the single best-fit recipe (R1 trim already landed) — the full `importYaml` (~1.5KB of commented YAML). `message` (p50 858B) is a prose re-render of the SAME options ("Options: 1. route="recipe" recipeSlug=… fit=… — <why verbatim>"). There is NO per-option executable `nextCall` in the current `action=start` path (0 of 265 rows carry `nextCalls`; only the deprecated `action=discover` legacy path had it).

2) SESSION-ACTIVE (`workflow:bootstrap/{classic,adopt,recipe}:start::session-active`; classic 154 rows p50 7.7KB, adopt 128 rows p50 5.1KB, recipe 63 rows p50 7.4KB). Top keys: `kind`, `sessionId`, `intent`, `progress{}`, `current{}`, `message`, `availableStacks`. The weight is `current.detailedGuide` (classic 6086B / recipe 5830B / adopt 2416B p50) — atom-synthesized markdown — plus `availableStacks` (1214B live stack catalog, present in 100% of rows for ALL three routes), plus a thin `message` ("Step 1/3: discover") and a 6-step `progress` array. `current.tools` and `current.verification` are the only machine-actionable hints; everything load-bearing about the NEXT call is buried in the `detailedGuide` prose.

ANNOTATED REAL EXAMPLE — `workflow:bootstrap/adopt:start::session-active` (5263 bytes, scenario launch-with-existing-cicd, suite 20260605-011606):
- `kind:"session-active"` + `sessionId` (18B) — machine state handle. GOOD.
- `progress{total:3,completed:0,steps:[discover/in_progress, provision/pending, close/pending]}` (~170B) — structured, useful.
- `current.verification` (~210B) — "SUCCESS WHEN: plan submitted via … action=complete step=discover" — the real next-action condition, structured-ish.
- `current.detailedGuide` (~2416B markdown) = `bootstrap-intro` atom ("Bootstrap is infrastructure-only … Three routes: Recipe/Classic/Adopt …") + `bootstrap-adopt-discover` atom which RE-EXPLAINS the very `action="start" workflow="bootstrap" route="adopt"` call the agent ALREADY made to receive this response, then explains the real next step (`complete step=discover scope=[...]`).
- `availableStacks` (1214B): the full live runtime+managed version catalog ("bun@1.3.9 (latest)·… postgresql@18 (latest)·17·16·14 …"). For ADOPT this is pure noise — adopt does not author a YAML or pick a type; its plan is derived from live discovery and `scope` is just a hostname list.
- `message:"Step 1/3: discover"` (20B).
So ~1.2KB (23%) of this adopt response is a stack-version menu the adopt route can never consume, and a chunk of the guide narrates a call already in the past.
families.headline: Every bootstrap session-active response ships the full 1214-byte live stack-version catalog (`availableStacks`) for all three routes — including adopt (which derives its plan from live discovery and only needs a hostname list) and recipe (where the recipe owns every service type) — making the single largest low-signal block a validation-set presented as a choice-menu the route can't use.

findings.title: availableStacks (1214B stack-version menu) ships on adopt + recipe session-active where no type is ever chosen from it
findings.claim: The stack catalog is gated only by step name (discover), not by route. So adopt and recipe session-active responses carry the full runtime+managed version list even though neither route authors a YAML from it: adopt derives its plan from live discovery with `scope=[hostnames]`, and recipe takes every `type` verbatim from the matched recipe's importYaml. The agent is handed the entire validation-set (every active version of every stack) as if it were a choice menu, at a decision point where the choice is already made by the route.
findings.payload_evidence: workflow:bootstrap/adopt:start::session-active (5263B) and workflow:bootstrap/recipe:start::session-active (7059B) both carry availableStacks=1214B verbatim: '## Available Service Stacks (live, active concrete versions)… Runtime: bun@1.3.9 (latest) · 1.2.2 …'. index.jsonl: availableStacks present in 128/128 adopt rows and 63/63 recipe rows (100%).
findings.rendering_owner: internal/tools/workflow_bootstrap.go:stackSteps (map has only StepDiscover, no route axis) → needsStacks → populateStacks; string built by internal/knowledge/versions_format.go:FormatStackList
findings.why_it_matters: Violates 'validation-set ≠ presentation-set' and 'recommend, don't enumerate': the full schema enum is for silent validation, not for showing the agent. On the adopt route the catalog is irrelevant to EVERY decision the agent makes; on recipe the recipe is the single owner of type. Presenting it invites the agent to second-guess the recipe's types or hand-pick versions adopt will never use — the exact over-provisioning misread Fit was introduced to prevent.
findings.proposed_direction: Gate availableStacks on route as well as step: emit it only for classic-route discover (the one route that authors types from intent). Drop it entirely from adopt and recipe session-active.

verdict.assessment:
PAYLOAD: Confirmed via index.jsonl + a live transcript. `availableStacks` is present in 128/128 adopt and 63/63 recipe `start::session-active` rows (100%, exactly the claimed count). The real content (extracted from eval/behavioral/runs/20260603-082235/adopt-existing-standard-pair/transcript.jsonl) starts `## Available Service Stacks (live, active concrete versions)` and carries the runtime+managed version list with `(latest)` markers — at `current.name == "discover"`. The quoted runtime fragment (`bun@1.3.9 (latest) · 1.2.2 …`) appears verbatim in the corpus (samples.md:340). Size caveat: 1214B is the MODAL byte size (43/128 adopt, 28/63 recipe), not invariant — sizes range 729–2273B with project/schema state; the finding's flat "1214B" is the plurality case, not wrong but should read "~729–2273B, 1214B modal".

CODE OWNER: Confirmed exactly. internal/tools/workflow_bootstrap.go:21 `stackSteps` map = {StepDiscover:true} with NO route axis; needsStacks (line 31-36) returns true purely on resp.Current.Name=="discover" regardless of route; populateStacks (line 291) calls knowledge.FormatStackList (versions_format.go:11) which builds the exact "## Available Service Stacks (live, active concrete versions)" string into resp.AvailableStacks. No route-conditional suppression exists anywhere in the start/complete/status handlers (bootstrapSessionRoute is available but never consulted for stack gating).

DEFECT IS REAL, not stylistic and not already-mitigated: adopt derives its plan from live discovery (adopt.go:107 BootstrapCompleteAdoptPlan — every adoptable runtime becomes isExisting, agent picks no type from the catalog); recipe derives from the matched recipe's import YAML (recipe_shape.go DeriveRecipePlan/InferRecipeShape — types taken from the recipe). On both routes the agent authors zero type from this menu, yet receives the full validation-set at discover. The existing one-shot mitigation (needsStacks false on completed/status responses, per its own doc-comment) fixes WRONG-TIME re-dumps but does NOT address this WRONG-ROUTE dump. Directly violates CLAUDE.md "validation-set ≠ presentation-set" / "recommend, don't enumerate". needsStacks's own comment ("where the agent is CHOOSING service types") is true only for the classic route — confirming the gate is mis-scoped.
verdict.corrected_claim: Substance holds; one numeric tightening: availableStacks is ~729–2273B depending on project state, with 1214B the modal size (43/128 adopt, 28/63 recipe rows) — state the range rather than a flat 1214B. The session-active field is rendered by FormatStackList (header "## Available Service Stacks (live, active concrete versions)"); the literal example string quoted in the finding is the sibling FormatServiceStacks briefing variant (header "## Service Stacks (live)") — same schema-derived catalog, different header, claim unaffected.

findings.title: Adopt session-active is ~1.2KB pure noise: availableStacks is 23% of the response and unusable by the route
findings.claim: For the adopt route the heaviest blocks are the least useful: availableStacks (1214B) cannot inform any adopt decision, and the detailedGuide's bootstrap-intro re-teaches the three-route taxonomy after the agent already committed to adopt. The decision-critical bytes for the adopt next action are a single line ('complete step=discover scope=["appdev","appstage"]') buried in ~2.4KB of guide.
findings.payload_evidence: adopt session-active p50=5063B (index.jsonl): current(detailedGuide) p50=2416B + availableStacks 1214B + intro/message/progress. The one load-bearing instruction is inside bootstrap-adopt-discover.md: 'zerops_workflow action="complete" step="discover" scope=["appdev","appstage"]'.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/workflow/bootstrap_guide_assembly.go:buildGuide (atom synthesis) + internal/tools/workflow_bootstrap.go:populateStacks; intro from internal/content/atoms/bootstrap-intro.md
findings.why_it_matters: Signal-to-noise on the route's first response is poor: the agent parses 5KB to extract a one-line scope call, and the largest single block (the version catalog) is decision-irrelevant for adopt. Correct-but-buried = not a correct tell under the lens.
findings.proposed_direction: Drop availableStacks for adopt (per finding above) and demote bootstrap-intro to a one-line route-confirm once a route is committed; lead the adopt guide with the scope= call.

verdict.assessment: PAYLOAD: Verified against plans/response-audit-corpus/index.jsonl (131 adopt:start entries) and samples/workflow-bootstrap-adopt-start-session-active.json. index shows bytes p50=5059 (claim 5063, match), availableStacks=1214B appears x43 (exact match), current=2416B appears x19 (match). Canonical sample measures availableStacks=1173 raw chars = 22.3% of 5263 total; detailedGuide=3248 chars. The "23% of response" claim rounds correctly from both 24.0% (corpus p50) and 22.3% (canonical). CODE OWNER: Confirmed exactly as cited. internal/tools/workflow_bootstrap.go populateStacks (l.291) injects AvailableStacks; needsStacks (l.31-36) gates on stackSteps map which is keyed ONLY on step name "discover" (l.20-23) with NO route awareness — so adopt's discover step gets the full type catalog. handleBootstrapStart (workflow.go:1007) attaches it because BootstrapStartWithRoute lands adopt on discover; the doc-comment l.1003-1006 even states the intent ("where the agent chooses types"). detailedGuide assembled by bootstrap_guide_assembly.go:buildGuide from atom corpus; intro from internal/content/atoms/bootstrap-intro.md (priority:0, leads with "Three routes: Recipe/Classic/Adopt" taxonomy); load-bearing scope call lives at internal/content/atoms/bootstrap-adopt-discover.md:33. DEFECT IS REAL not stylistic: BootstrapCompleteAdoptPlan (adopt.go:135-165) derives each adopted service's type from the LIVE existing service's ServiceStackTypeVersionName — the agent only names hostnames in scope, never picks a type from a catalog, so the type-version catalog cannot inform any adopt decision. BURIAL CONFIRMED WHERE: scope call sits at char offset 2070/3248 (63% into detailedGuide), AFTER the full three-route taxonomy intro the agent already passed by committing to adopt. MINOR IMPRECISION: finding labels current p50 as ~2.4KB (2416B, a real older-variant corpus value x19) but the live canonical content is larger (detailedGuide alone 3248B, current 3683B) — this understates and thus strengthens, not weakens, the burial claim.
verdict.corrected_claim: Claim holds with one numeric label refined: the detailedGuide on the current/live adopt response is ~3.2KB (not ~2.4KB); 2416B is a real but older corpus variant. The 1214B availableStacks (~23% of the ~5KB response) and the 63%-buried scope call are accurate for the live payload. Net: availableStacks is route-irrelevant noise (step-only gating, no route awareness) and the one load-bearing instruction sits past the three-route taxonomy the agent already resolved.

findings.title: Route-menu hands the agent prose to reconstruct the second start call instead of an executable nextCall object
findings.claim: In the current action=start route-menu path the agent must build the route-commit call ('call zerops_workflow action="start" workflow="bootstrap" route="<route>"' with the right recipeSlug + threaded intent) by reading the prose `message`. The structured `routeOptions[]` carry route/recipeSlug/fit but NO ready-to-pass `nextCall` args map. The better shape — a per-option nextCalls[] with the full verbatim args — existed in the legacy action=discover path and was dropped from the production start path.
findings.payload_evidence: workflow:bootstrap:start::route-menu: 0 of 265 rows carry nextCalls (top_keys = intent/kind/message/projectId/routeOptions only). The deprecated workflow:bootstrap:discover::route-menu sample DOES carry nextCalls[] with full args {action,intent,recipeSlug,route,workflow} 'agents pass it through verbatim'.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/workflow/route.go:BootstrapRouteOption (no NextCall field) + internal/workflow/engine.go:buildDiscoveryMessage (prose-only commit instructions)
findings.why_it_matters: Reachability + structured-execution: the one action the agent must take next is delivered as prose it must parse and recompose (route name, slug, intent re-threading), a known source of slug/intent transcription errors, instead of an object it executes. The capability already exists and regressed out of the live path.
findings.proposed_direction: Add a per-option executable nextCall (full args incl. threaded intent + recipeSlug) to each routeOption, mirroring the legacy discover path; the message prose then becomes optional pick-one framing.

verdict.assessment: Payload: verified exact. 265 `workflow:bootstrap:start::route-menu` rows in plans/response-audit-corpus/index.jsonl, 0 carry nextCalls; top_keys = [intent, kind, message, projectId, routeOptions] (262 rows) / [kind, message, projectId, routeOptions] (3 rows). The single `discover::route-menu` sample (suite 20260509-061753, plans/response-audit-corpus/samples/workflow-bootstrap-discover-route-menu.json) DOES carry nextCalls[] with full args {action,intent,recipeSlug,route,workflow} and the message literal "agents pass it through verbatim". Code owner: verified exact. internal/workflow/route.go:122 BootstrapRouteOption has no NextCall/NextCalls field; internal/workflow/bootstrap.go:121 BootstrapDiscoveryResponse has exactly 5 fields (Kind/Intent/ProjectID/RouteOptions/Message), no nextCalls; internal/workflow/engine.go:429 buildDiscoveryMessage produces prose commit instructions containing the literal placeholder route="<route>" plus inline-enumerated options. Defect is real: engine.go:995 BootstrapStartWithRoute takes input.Intent on the SECOND call and no session exists yet at route-menu time, so intent is not server-persisted — the agent must assemble {action,workflow,route,recipeSlug,intent} from three places (top-level intent verbatim string + per-option route + per-option recipeSlug) with no single passable object; this is the structured-execution/transcription-risk class the discover message named and the start path lacks. One framing correction that does NOT weaken the defect: `git log -S nextCalls`/`-S NextCalls` across --all is EMPTY — nextCalls was never in committed Go source; the May-9 discover sample came from an uncommitted/experimental binary in a gitignored eval run, so it was a prototype, not a shipped-then-regressed capability. The defect stands on current committed code regardless. Not buried/not stale-bool — confirmed the prose message IS the only commit-instruction carrier and intent is NOT recovered server-side. Severity refined high→medium: routeOptions[] DO carry route+recipeSlug per option (not pure prose), and the corpus shows 20 start::obj committed-route responses, so agents demonstrably complete the second call — real friction and a known slug/intent transcription surface, but not a hard block.
verdict.corrected_claim: Holds on the substance. Correct the "existed in the legacy action=discover path and was dropped from the production start path" framing: nextCalls never existed in committed Go source (git log -S across --all is empty); the discover sample that carries it came from an uncommitted/experimental binary in a gitignored May-9 eval run. The accurate framing is "a verbatim-passable nextCalls object was prototyped in an off-tree binary and never made it into the shipped route-menu response; the production start::route-menu path delivers the route-commit call as prose the agent must recompose (substitute route="<route>", copy the matching recipeSlug, re-thread the verbatim intent) with no executable object on any code path, current or historical-committed."

findings.title: Route-menu message re-renders routeOptions as prose (why/fit/recipeSlug duplicated structured + text)
findings.claim: The `message` field re-emits each option's route/recipeSlug/fit and the FULL verbatim `why` string that already lives structured in routeOptions[]. The same why text is shipped twice per option (once in routeOptions[i].why, once in message 'Options: i. … — <why>'). This is a surface-twice duplication that grows linearly with option count.
findings.payload_evidence: route-menu sample: routeOptions[0].why = 'A minimal Next.js 15 application using standalone output mode…' AND message contains '1. route="recipe" recipeSlug="nextjs-ssr-hello-world" fit="exact" — A minimal Next.js 15 application using standalone output mode…' verbatim. message p50=858B, routeOptions p50=2337B across 265 rows.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/workflow/engine.go:buildDiscoveryMessage (loops options, re-prints opt.Why) — set alongside RouteOptions in engine.go BootstrapResponse assembly (~line 314)
findings.why_it_matters: Two copies of the same fact in one response is a tell==tell drift hazard (edit one, forget the other) and pure token tax. Under 'surface once', the rationale should live in exactly one place — the structured field the agent reads, not also re-narrated.
findings.proposed_direction: Shrink message to a single framing sentence + 'pick an option from routeOptions and invoke its nextCall'; stop re-printing per-option why/fit (already structured).

findings.title: The real next-action condition sits in current.verification / detailedGuide prose, not a top-level nextCall field
findings.claim: On session-active the agent's next action (complete step=discover with the route-appropriate input) is communicated via `current.verification` ('SUCCESS WHEN: plan submitted via zerops_workflow action=complete step=discover…') and elaborated only inside the multi-KB detailedGuide. There is no top-level structured nextCall the agent executes; message says only 'Step 1/3: discover'. For classic the load-bearing 'stageHostname MUST be inside runtime' and the example JSON are several hundred bytes deep in detailedGuide.
findings.payload_evidence: classic session-active (7693B): current.verification present but the actionable plan template ('[{"runtime":{"devHostname":"appdev","stageHostname":"appstage",…}}]') is embedded in detailedGuide at ~6KB depth; message=20B 'Step 1/3: discover'.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/workflow/bootstrap.go:BuildResponse / Current.DetailedGuide (line ~301) assembled by internal/workflow/bootstrap_guide_assembly.go:buildGuide
findings.why_it_matters: Decision-head reachability: the one structured field that names the next call (verification) is a success-condition string, not an executable; the concrete shape the agent must produce is below-the-fold prose. An LLM that stops reading early or compacts the guide loses the exact plan shape.
findings.proposed_direction: Promote a structured nextStep/nextCall skeleton (action=complete, step=discover, plan/scope shape per route) to a top-level field so the agent executes rather than scrapes it out of the guide.

findings.title: bootstrap-intro re-teaches the three-route taxonomy AFTER the route is already committed
findings.claim: Every session-active detailedGuide opens with the bootstrap-intro atom ('Bootstrap is infrastructure-only … Three routes: Recipe / Classic / Adopt …'). But session-active only exists because the agent ALREADY chose a route in the start call — enumerating the other two routes at this point is post-decision noise that the route-specific atom then repeats more concretely.
findings.payload_evidence: All three session-active samples begin identically: 'Bootstrap is **infrastructure-only**… Three routes: - **Recipe**… - **Classic**… - **Adopt**…' (bootstrap-intro.md verbatim), followed by the route-specific block. The intro is ~600B repeated across classic/adopt/recipe.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/content/atoms/bootstrap-intro.md (phases:[bootstrap-active] steps:[discover], no route filter) synthesized by internal/workflow/bootstrap_guide_assembly.go:buildGuide
findings.why_it_matters: WHAT-per-type mismatch: a route-menu-era taxonomy is being delivered inside the post-commit response. It tells the agent about routes it can no longer pick, diluting the route-specific instructions it actually needs.
findings.proposed_direction: Restrict bootstrap-intro to the route-menu / no-route-committed surface; on session-active lead directly with the committed route's atom (a one-line 'route=adopt committed' header is enough).

findings.title: availableStacks IS live-truth (schema cache) — confirming the defect is relevance, not staleness
findings.claim: Auditing TIMING for completeness: availableStacks derives from schemaCache.Get(ctx) (live, host-derived, 15-min TTL, poison-guarded), so its CONTENT is current platform truth — not a stale snapshot. The importYaml in route-menu comes from the curated recipe corpus doc (static template, correctly so). So no stale-bool bug hides here; the availableStacks problem is purely reachability/relevance (it ships where the route can't use it), which the other findings cover.
findings.payload_evidence: FormatStackList header: '## Available Service Stacks (live, active concrete versions)'; fed by schemaCache.Get(ctx) in populateStacks. routeOptions[].importYaml sourced from doc.ImportYAML (recipe corpus), not a live platform read.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/knowledge/versions_format.go:FormatStackList ← internal/tools/workflow_bootstrap.go:populateStacks(schemaCache.Get(ctx))
findings.why_it_matters: Closes the TIMING dimension honestly: the live-truth contract is satisfied for these fields, so fixes should target delivery (where/whether to ship), not freshness.
findings.proposed_direction: No timing change needed; treat availableStacks as a routing/relevance problem per the RIGHT_INFO and HOW_MUCH findings.

families.anatomy:
PER-RESPONSE CONTENT MAP (rendering owner: internal/workflow/bootstrap.go::BootstrapState.BuildResponse, which fills the BootstrapResponse struct; detailedGuide assembled by internal/workflow/bootstrap_guide_assembly.go::buildGuide via Synthesize→BodiesOf; terminal close message by BuildTransitionMessage):

(A) workflow:complete:discover::session-active (p50 5078 B, current=4980 avg). Top keys: kind, sessionId, intent, progress{total,completed,steps[]}, current{name,index,tools[],verification,detailedGuide,priorContext{plan,attestations},planMode}, message. The `current` block describes the NEXT step (after discover completes, current.name="provision"). detailedGuide ≈ 3.5 KB of fixed procedure prose PLUS the full recipe import YAML re-embedded. Next-action ("call zerops_import with services: only") is sentence ~6 of the prose.

(B) workflow:complete:provision::session-active (p50 3405 B, current=4326 avg). Same shape; current.name="close". Adds checkResult{passed,checks[],summary} (257 B) + autoMounts[] (82 B). detailedGuide for the close step is ~2 KB telling the agent to run zerops_discover and NOT run zerops_verify — yet current.verification says only "SUCCESS WHEN: bootstrap administratively closed (metas written...)". The tell (guide: go discover+inspect) and the success-criterion field (verification: administratively closed) describe different actions.

(C) workflow:complete:close::session-active (p50 1136 B, message=727 avg). TERMINAL: current is nil — NO tools[], NO verification, NO structured next field. Entire next-action is markdown inside `message` (rendered by BuildTransitionMessage). intent + full progress[] still re-emitted.

ANNOTATED REAL EXAMPLE — (A), scenario api-node-postgres-classic-dev, 5078 bytes, verbatim structure:

  "intent":"Node.js REST API s PostgreSQL... žádné stage/produkce" (125 B — full free-text user goal, RE-EMITTED every complete turn)
  "progress":{total:3,completed:1,steps:[discover=complete,provision=in_progress,close=pending]} (171 B — full array re-emitted every turn)
  "current":{ name:"provision", index:1,
     "tools":["zerops_import","zerops_process","zerops_discover"]  ← flat 3-tool menu, no order, no "call X first"
     "verification":"SUCCESS WHEN: all plan services exist in API with ACTIVE/RUNNING..."  ← success criterion, separate from guide
     "detailedGuide":"### Provision recipe services\n... 1. Project-level env vars... 2. Import services. Strip project:. Submit services: verbatim via zerops_import... 3. Wait until every service reaches a running state... 4. Record discovered env vars... \n## Recipe — nodejs-hello-world\n```yaml\nproject:\n  name:...\nservices:\n  - hostname: appdev\n    type: nodejs@22..."  ← ~3.5 KB; the literal next call lives in step 2 of the prose; full import YAML re-embedded
     "priorContext":{plan:{targets:[...]}, attestations:{discover:"Planned targets..."}}  ← prior plan+attestation re-dumped
  }
  "message":"Derived plan from recipe nodejs-hello-world: appdev.\n\nStep 2/3: provision"  ← the one machine-cheap pointer, but it just names the step, not the call.
families.headline: Across all three bootstrap-complete responses the agent's single load-bearing next-action (which tool to call, in what order, with what success criterion) is never a structured executable field — it is prose buried inside a 3–5 KB detailedGuide markdown blob (or, at close, a 727-byte message blob), while a flat unordered tools[] menu and a free-text verification string sit above it without saying what to do first.

findings.title: No structured nextCall — the agent's next tool invocation is prose it must parse, never a field it executes
findings.claim: Every bootstrap-complete response advertises the next step via a flat tools[] string array plus a free-text verification string, but the actual instruction (which of the listed tools to call first, with which arguments, in what order) exists only as numbered prose inside detailedGuide. There is no nextCall object the agent can execute without parsing markdown. At terminal close there is not even a tools[] — the next call is a markdown sentence inside a 727-byte message.
findings.payload_evidence: workflow:complete:discover::session-active (5078 B): current.tools=["zerops_import","zerops_process","zerops_discover"] is unordered; the real first call is detailedGuide step 2 'Submit services: verbatim via zerops_import'. workflow:complete:close::session-active (1136 B): message="...Next: `zerops_workflow action=\"start\" workflow=\"develop\"` — develop owns scaffolding..." — no structured field.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/workflow/bootstrap.go:293 BootstrapState.BuildResponse (fills current.Tools/Verification/DetailedGuide); internal/workflow/bootstrap_guide_assembly.go:23 buildGuide (prose); :318 BuildTransitionMessage (close message)
findings.why_it_matters: Violates STRUCTURED-vs-PROSE and RIGHT-INFO-RIGHT-TIME: an LLM acting on these must read and parse 3.5 KB to reconstruct one tool call instead of executing a typed object. A nextCall the agent EXECUTES rather than reads is the difference between deterministic and parse-dependent behavior; the tools[] menu is the validation-set presented as the choice-set.
findings.proposed_direction: Add a structured current.nextCall{tool, args, successCriterion} carrying the single recommended first call; demote tools[] to validation/reference and let detailedGuide remain depth-only.

verdict.assessment:
PAYLOAD: Both cited payloads exist exactly. The 5078 B discover payload is at index.jsonl:4642 (suite 20260604-204822, scenario api-node-postgres-classic-dev) and is captured verbatim in samples/workflow-complete-discover-session-active.json — current.tools=["zerops_import","zerops_process","zerops_discover"], a flat unordered string array; verification is a free-text SUCCESS-WHEN string; detailedGuide is numbered prose with the import step embedded mid-text plus the full recipe YAML. The 1136 B close payload is at index.jsonl:4676/5120 (greenfield-fullstack-multi-runtime) and in samples/workflow-complete-close-session-active.json — top_keys are [intent,kind,message,progress,sessionId] with NO current/tools[] key at terminal close; the next call exists only as the markdown sentence inside the message (component 771 B, claim said 727 — minor off-by-44 overstatement, directionally correct).

CODE OWNER: Confirmed, line numbers slightly drifted but symbols real. internal/workflow/bootstrap.go:270 BootstrapState.BuildResponse fills Current.Tools=detail.Tools (line 296, a STATIC []string from stepDetails in bootstrap_steps.go:20-31), Current.Verification=detail.Verification (static, line 297), and Current.DetailedGuide=b.buildGuide(...) (prose, line 301). The close message is produced by bootstrap_guide_assembly.go:318 BuildTransitionMessage — its line 358 emits the exact verbatim string in the close payload ("Next: `zerops_workflow action=\"start\" workflow=\"develop\"` — develop owns scaffolding..."). families.anatomy:
The develop family splits cleanly into ONE prose monolith and FIVE well-structured JSON mutations — a within-family delivery schism.

(1) workflow:develop:start::prose — THE WALL. Produced by `internal/tools/workflow_develop.go:renderDevelopBriefing` → `workflow.RenderStatus(...)` wrapped in `textResult()` (convert.go:114). It is a single markdown string; ALL 265 instances carry `top_keys:[]` / `components:{_text}` — zero structured fields. Content map (measured on the 15,599-byte greenfield-website sample): `## Status` head (phase+intent line); `Services:` block (one line/service with bootstrapped/mode/closeMode/gitPush/buildIntegration/deployed axes); `→ Auto-close blocked: N/M ready … Next: zerops_deploy targetService="app"` blocker line at byte 567 (3% down — the early next-action); then `Guidance:` = ~14,676 bytes across 12 `### ` atom sections (sizes: first-deploy-branch 1629, where-values-come-from 1279, self-shadow 625, env-catalog 1056, establish-zerops.yaml 1599, http-diagnostics 1472, static-runtime 1841, self-deploy-destruction 1126, knowledge-on-demand 658, auto-close 634, run-first-deploy 1391, verify-matrix 1366) + 4 `pull on demand` pointers; finally a `Next:` Plan block at byte 15,392 (99% down) with `▸ Primary: Deploy app — zerops_deploy targetService="app"`. The atoms are selected by `workflow.Synthesize` (synthesize.go) from a 61-atom develop-active corpus, ordered by priority, rendered into bodies via `BodiesOf` — NOT passed through `ComposeUnderBudget`.

(2-6) The mutation responses are exemplary structured JSON via `jsonResult`: close-mode (workflow_close_mode.go, 420B, top_keys services/status/workSessionState), record-deploy (workflow_record_deploy.go, 571B, typed stamped/firstDeployedAt/subdomainUrl/workSessionState), build-integration (workflow_build_integration.go, 4143B, typed secrets[]/ghAuthPrecondition/workflowFile.content/topologyNote), set-default-setup (workflow_set_default_setup.go, 91B), git-push-setup walkthrough (workflow_git_push_setup.go, 7001B, typed inputsRequired[]/steps[]/nextStep/recommendedIntegration).

VERIFIED against real payload + code owner; the finding holds.

PAYLOAD (plans/response-audit-corpus/index.jsonl + samples/workflow-develop-start-prose.json):
- kind="workflow:develop:start::prose" — confirmed 265 occurrences (most-frequent develop response).
- ALL 265: top_keys=[], is_json=false, components={_text:N} — pure markdown string, no JSON structure. Verified by jq/grep over the full index.

The substance — instruction exists ONLY as prose at start + end — holds exactly.

CODE OWNER (internal/tools/workflow_develop.go:270 renderDevelopBriefing):
- Returns `textResult(workflow.RenderStatus(...)), nil, nil`. RenderStatus (internal/workflow/render.go:26) returns a plain string; renderPlan (line 385) flattens via `fmt.Fprintf(b, "  ▸ Primary: %s\n", formatAction(plan.Primary))`. textResult (convert.go:114) wraps it as a single TextContent. The structured second return value is nil. So the agent receives ONLY markdown.
- DECISIVE: at the call site `plan := workflow.BuildPlan(envelope)` builds workflow.Plan, whose struct (plan.go:19) ALREADY carries full JSON tags — Primary.Tool + Primary.Args(map[string]string) — i.e. the exact nextCall:{tool,args} object the finding says is missing. Its docstring calls it "the typed replacement for today's free-form Next section ... the ONLY source of what should happen next in any tool response." This typed object is built, serialized to prose, and discarded. Not unavailable — deliberately thrown away here.

CONTRAST (refutation attempt failed): the develop work-session's sibling mutation responses ARE typed JSON — git-push-setup::status=walkthrough carries typed nextStep+steps+inputsRequired+workSessionState (is_json=true); record-deploy::obj carries stamped/workSessionState/firstDeployedAt (is_json=true). Same lifecycle, structured form is the norm; develop:start is the one denied it.

NOT mitigated: the next call is reachable only by regexing prose out of a 9-32KB blob. REACHABILITY/STRUCTURED-vs-PROSE violation is real and impairs the agent (truncation/misparse risk on the heaviest, most action-critical response).

One framing imprecision (does not change verdict): the finding calls the contrast "the same family's five MUTATION responses." git-push-setup/record-deploy are emitted under kind prefix workflow:?: not workflow:develop:, so they're develop-SESSION-lifecycle peers, not literally the develop:start::* sub-family. The contrast's substance (typed JSON is used everywhere else in this flow) is fully correct.

families.anatomy:
The launch-production family is a STATELESS MULTI-CALL NARROWING state machine. Every advance is `zerops_workflow action="start" workflow="launch-production"` carrying the full accumulated `inputs`; the server re-derives status each call (scope-prompt → source-control-required → classify-prompt → ready-to-launch → launching → launched|failed). A separate read-only `action="status"` path recovers mid-flight launches.

Per response-kind content map (all owned by internal/tools/workflow_launch_production.go unless noted):

Owner: launchScopePromptResponse.

2. status=source-control-required (6.6KB, recent): guidance=4898B atom `launch-source-control-required` (a SIX-ROW disambiguation table covering every possible blocker), blockers=760B (the ACTUAL active blockers, each with id+severity+category+message+recovery{tool,action,args}), sourceContext=233B, inputs=55B. 3. status=classify-prompt (8.5KB, recent): guidance=7595B atom `launch-classify-prompt` (four-bucket table + worked examples + mis-classification traps), classifications=518B (per-env rows: key + suggestedBucket + rationale, computed server-side from key NAME), sourceContext=264B. 4. status::launch-active (2KB) via action="status": top-level STRUCTURED fields kind="launch-active", status, launchId, sourceProjectId, targetProjectName, targetServiceHostname, lastUpdate (all LIVE from state file), ambiguousChoices[] (when >1 active), guidance=1612B atom `launch-status-recovery`, and crucially `nextCall`=87B — a ready-to-execute call string. verdict.assessment:
PAYLOAD: Confirmed exactly in eval/behavioral/runs/20260521-102710/launch-production-dev-only/transcript.jsonl (and 20+ sibling launch-production runs in index.jsonl, kind=workflow:launch-production:start::status=source-control-required). blockers[].recovery for git-push-unconfigured-api = {"tool":"zerops_workflow","action":"git-push-setup","args":{"service":"api"}}; remote-mismatch adds remoteUrl, no gitToken. The DEFECT claim is REFUTED on three counts:

(1) The premise "guidance prose states remoteUrl/gitToken are required [on the recovery call]" is FALSE. I read the embedded 4.4KB guidance table in the same payload. The git-push-unconfigured row's recovery cell is literally `zerops_workflow action="git-push-setup" service="<hostname>"` — NO remoteUrl/gitToken — with "collect the user's repo URL + PAT + CI choice, THEN re-call launch." The remote-mismatch row shows `service + remoteUrl` only. The prose and the recovery struct AGREE; there is no drift, so the one-owner/STRUCTURED-vs-PROSE premise has no basis.

(2) "Recovery cannot be executed as-is" is FALSE. handleGitPushSetup (internal/tools/workflow_git_push_setup.go:149) is a deliberate TWO-MODE handler: when RemoteURL=="" (walkthrough) it returns status="walkthrough" + an inputsRequired typed-picker block collecting remoteUrl/gitToken/integration; only when RemoteURL is set does it enter confirm mode. The WorkflowInput.RemoteURL jsonschema tag (workflow.go:56) states verbatim "Omit on first call to receive env-aware setup atom"; GitToken (line 58) is "Required when remoteUrl is set" — conditional, not first-call. So {service:"api"} IS the complete, canonical, documented first call — it fires the collection flow, which is the intended path, not an error.

families.anatomy:
The export family is a stateless 3-call narrowing (probe → generate → publish) on `zerops_workflow workflow="export"`. Every non-error response is a flat JSON object with the same skeleton: `status` (string enum), `phase` ("export-active"), `targetService` (hostname), `guidance` (a markdown blob composed from 1-3 atoms), `nextSteps` (string array of copy-paste commands), plus status-specific structured fields. The rendering split is owned by `internal/tools/workflow_export.go` per-status builders (`classifyPromptResponse`, `validationFailedResponse`, `composeReadyResponse`, `publishGuidanceResponse`, `scopePromptResponse`); `guidance` is rendered by `internal/workflow/synthesize_export.go::RenderExportGuidance` from atoms filtered on the `exportStatus:` axis (`internal/content/atoms/export-*.md`); the env table's `suggestedBucket`/`rationale` come from `internal/tools/classify_envs.go::suggestBucketForKey` → `internal/topology/env_classification.go` (single owner, shared with the composer).

Per response-type content map:
- scope-prompt (~no recent sample, builder at workflow_export.go::scopePromptResponse): status + guidance(export-intro+export-scope-prompt ~3.9KB) + nextSteps. Asks which runtime hostname to export.
- classify-prompt (23.7KB, the single largest non-knowledge response): structured `envClassificationTable` (one row/env: key, currentBucket, suggestedBucket, rationale — 518B for 3 envs), `fetchValuesVia` (75B command), `warnings` (309B, per-env "not classified" notes), `zeropsYaml` (4208B verbatim live file), `nextSteps` (120B) — PLUS `guidance` of 18282B (export-intro 2.4KB + export-classify-envs 9.9KB + export-validate 6.4KB).
- validation-failed (13.9KB): `errors` (96B: path+message), `preview` (5079B: both YAMLs + repoUrl + setupName + zeropsYamlSource), `guidance` 8306B (export-intro 2.4KB + export-validate 6.4KB), nextSteps 163B.
- compose-ready (7.6KB): `bundle` (5058B: importYaml+zeropsYaml+setupName+repoUrl+warnings+filenames), `guidance` 2212B (export-intro only), nextSteps 269B. Terminal deliverable when git-push not configured.
- git-push-setup-required (11.9KB): guidance 6735B + preview 4786B. publish-ready: bundle + guidance + 4 SSH/deploy nextSteps. error (384B): code+error+suggestion+recovery{tool,action:status}.

ANNOTATED REAL EXAMPLE — classify-prompt (kind=workflow:export:start::status=classify-prompt, 23768 bytes, from export-buildfromgit-self-snapshot suite 20260604-192113):

families.anatomy:
This family has three structurally distinct delivery shapes, and the split itself is the story:

(1) verify (single-service) — STRUCTURED JSON. Owner: internal/tools/verify.go::RegisterVerify → verifyResponse{*ops.VerifyResult, Note, WorkSessionState}, marshalled via jsonResult (convert.go:102). Content map: hostname/type/typeVersion/runtimeClass/runtimeClassification (identity, ~110B) + status (degraded/healthy/unhealthy) + checks[] (the pass/fail DECISION, each CheckResult{name,status,detail,httpStatus,recovery?,bodyText?,consoleErrors?}) + workSessionState{status,progress{ready,total,pending,autoCloseStatus,reason}} (the lifecycle/auto-close signal). All live-probed (ListServices + live GET /). The Recovery struct (tool+action+args) lives INSIDE the failing check, which is correct placement.

(2) verify-all — same shape wrapped as verifyAllResult{summary,status,services[]VerifyResult} + workSessionState; services[] is N full per-service results (avg 3504B, max 6510B).

(3) workflow:?:status::prose — PROSE. Owner: internal/tools/workflow.go::handleLifecycleStatus → it computes a fully-typed StateEnvelope + typed Plan (BuildPlan→NextAction{Label,Tool,Args,Rationale}) + guidance atoms, then COLLAPSES all three into one markdown string via textResult(workflow.RenderStatus(...)) (render.go:26). The corpus labels this _text (zero structured keys). This is the documented compaction-recovery primitive, p50=6.5KB, max=20.7KB.

(4) reset — STRUCTURED JSON, the clean counter-example. Owner: workflow.go::handleReset → jsonResult(resetResult{cleared,preserved}), 152B: {"cleared":{"bootstrapSessionId":...,"completedSteps":1,"incompleteMetas":["appdev"]},"preserved":{"liveServices":11}}. Terse, typed, no prose, no re-dump.

ANNOTATED REAL EXAMPLE — verify, 1140 bytes (samples/verify.json, greenfield-fullstack-multi-runtime), the http_root failure path the agent must act on:
{"hostname":"apidev","type":"runtime","typeVersion":"alpine/nodejs@22","runtimeClass":"dynamic","runtimeClassification":"classified HTTP runtime from deployed setup \"apidev\" (has HTTP)",  ← 110B identity/provenance block, reference-only

The agent cannot execute the next call; it must parse the tool name and args back out of text. The launch-active status path proves this is solvable in-family: it emits a structured nextCall string field. The develop/idle status path — the actual compaction-recovery primitive — does not.

The entire next-step is the trailing line 'Next:\n  ▸ Primary: Adopt unmanaged runtimes — zerops_workflow action="start" route="adopt" workflow="bootstrap"'. Contrast samples/workflow-status-launch-active.json (1967B) which carries top-level "nextCall":"zerops_workflow workflow=\"launch-production\" productionProjectName=\"api-prod\"" as a structured field.

Typed source thrown away: internal/workflow/plan.go::NextAction{Tool,Args}.
findings.why_it_matters: Violates STRUCTURED-vs-PROSE and the lens's reachability principle at the worst possible point: status is THE supported recovery-after-compaction surface (CLAUDE.md 'Lifecycle recovery is via action=status'). After compaction the agent has lost conversation context and must reconstruct its next move from this single response — handing it prose it must parse instead of a nextCall object it can execute directly maximises the chance of a malformed recovery call.
findings.proposed_direction: Emit status as structured JSON (phase + progress + blockers[] + plan.primary/alternatives as typed nextCall objects), like the launch-active and reset paths already do; keep a rendered _text only as an optional human mirror, never as the sole carrier of the next action.

findings.title: Status next-action sits below 6KB of route-menu prose; the route walkthroughs are emitted even when the route is already decided
findings.claim: RenderStatus orders sections Phase→Services→Progress→Blockers→Guidance→Next. The load-bearing 'Next:' pointer is rendered LAST, after the full Guidance dump (the route-menu atom: two-phase bootstrap, coexistence, ranked-options table, explicit-overrides, collision-semantics, FIRST-CALL adopt block, etc.). The agent must scroll past ~6KB of multi-route pedagogy to reach the one action. The Guidance presents the entire validation-set of routes (adopt/recipe/classic/resume) as a choice menu even when phase already implies a single next step.
findings.payload_evidence: workflow:?:status::prose, 7112B (samples/workflow-status-prose.json): 5 '###' guidance sections (Bootstrap is two-phase / Coexistence / Ranked options table / Explicit overrides / Collision semantics) precede the single trailing 'Next:\n  ▸ Primary: Adopt unmanaged runtimes'. The lens: 'a correct fact buried below the fold is not a correct tell.' On compaction recovery the agent reads top-down; the action it needs is dead last behind a route firehose it must filter.
findings.proposed_direction: Hoist the decision-head (phase + one recommended nextCall + blockers) above Guidance; demote the multi-route walkthrough to a single recommended route (or a pointer the agent fetches only when ambiguous).

findings.title: Status re-dumps byte-identical guidance every turn (surface-once violation)
findings.claim: Successive action=status calls in the same session re-emit the identical multi-KB guidance block. The guidance is selected purely from the envelope/phase with no memory of what was already shown, so an agent polling status during an iteration loop receives the same 2-6KB route/coexistence prose on every call.
findings.payload_evidence: greenfield-website-from-brief status::prose turns 14 and 24 are byte-identical at 2347 bytes ({_text:2347} both). launch-production-pipeline-not-configured emits the same 6034-byte prose across multiple turn-1 status calls. delivery-git-push-actions-setup status turn 13 reaches 20714 bytes.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/tools/workflow.go::handleLifecycleStatus → workflow.Synthesize + BodiesOf (no surfaced-once dedup); renderGuidance in render.go:354 dumps whatever bodies it is handed.
findings.why_it_matters: Violates surface-once ('don't re-dump every turn'). Re-paying 2-6KB of unchanged pedagogy on every status poll wastes context budget and trains the agent to skim/ignore the status response — corroding the one surface that must stay legible for recovery.
findings.proposed_direction: Guidance dedup keyed on session: emit the full route/coexistence atoms once per session, then a one-line 'guidance unchanged' marker on repeat status calls; always re-emit the small live decision-head (phase/progress/nextCall).

findings.title: Status recovery primitive balloons to 20KB — a recovery surface should be the tightest, not the largest
findings.claim: The status::prose kind, documented as the compaction-recovery primitive, has no payload ceiling on its prose path and reaches 20714 bytes in a real run. ComposeUnderBudget demotes atoms but the resulting markdown still dwarfs the structured alternatives (reset=152B, launch-active=1967B with the same lifecycle role).
findings.payload_evidence: workflow:?:status::prose max=20714 bytes (delivery-git-push-actions-setup turn 13, {_text:20714}); p50=7112. Compare reset (samples/workflow-reset-obj.json, 152B structured) and status::launch-active (1967B structured nextCall) carrying equivalent lifecycle/recovery intent.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/tools/workflow.go::handleLifecycleStatus (ComposeUnderBudget at line 1079 bounds atom bodies but the markdown envelope is unbounded) → render.go::RenderStatus.
findings.why_it_matters: Violates HOW-MUCH and the timing/recovery contract: the response the agent leans on after losing context is the heaviest, lowest-signal-density one in the family. A 20KB markdown recovery payload is the opposite of what a just-compacted agent can act on cleanly.
findings.proposed_direction: Cap the recovery-head to a small structured object (phase/progress/blockers/nextCall) with a hard byte budget; relegate full atom guidance to an explicit fetch so the recovery primitive itself stays small and deterministic.

verdict.assessment:
PAYLOAD: confirmed exact. index.jsonl line 329 has workflow:?:status::prose bytes=20714, components {_text:20714}, turn 13, scenario delivery-git-push-actions-setup, suite 20260504-065807. Extracted the actual text from the transcript: a ~21KB markdown blob concatenating ~21 FULL atom bodies (Development&Deploy, "Read apiMeta on every error" with a full JSON example + 7-row markdown table, Two deploy classes, Picking deployFiles, Env var channels, HTTP diagnostics, Per-service verify matrix, Verdict protocol, etc.) — the entire develop-phase knowledge corpus dumped into one status response, with a single actionable "Next:" line. COMPARISONS: valid. reset::obj at 152B and status::launch-active at 1967B both exist in the corpus and both carry equivalent lifecycle/recovery intent (launch-active is literally the launch-production variant of the SAME action=status recovery primitive). The same lifecycle role is served structured at ~2KB in launch and as a 20KB+ markdown dump in develop — 10-130x heavier.

The structural defect (a documented compaction-recovery primitive permitted up to ~24KB+ of low-density guidance while siblings of the same role are 152B/1967B structured) is real and impairs a just-compacted agent. families.anatomy:
PER-RESPONSE-TYPE CONTENT MAP (per-tool family — what each kind actually ships):

• deploy (success, p50=780B, max=995B): flat JSON object. Head = status/mode/sourceService/targetService/targetServiceId/targetServiceType, then message (prose), then buildStatus/buildDuration/sshReady, then nextActions (prose string with an inline tool call), warnings[], subdomainAccessEnabled/subdomainUrl, workSessionState (progress sub-object). NO structured nextCall. Owner: internal/ops/deploy_common.go::DeployResult (struct field order = wire order).
• deploy (FAILURE, 33 cases, p50=3676B, max=7092B): SAME struct, but now buildLogs[] (avg 2409B) + buildLogsSource and/or runtimeLogs[] (avg 1817B) + runtimeLogsSource + failedPhase serialize in the MIDDLE (struct lines 27-31), and failureClassification (avg 559B: category/likelyCause/suggestedAction/signals) serializes LAST (struct line 52). suggestion (~353B) sits high (line 22). So the decision-head is suggestion (high) but the structured classification object the agent is told to read FIRST is below ~2KB of logs.
• discover (p50=1347B, max=11958B): {project, services[], warnings[]}. Each service = hostname/serviceId/type/status/mode/adoptionState/isInfrastructure/subdomainEnabled. warnings[] re-emits a 513B adoptable-services paragraph whenever any service is adoptable. Owner: internal/tools/discover.go (warning at line 132).
• import (p50=825B): {projectId, projectName, processes[], summary, nextActions(prose)}. Owner: internal/ops/import.go.
• knowledge (p50=5618B, max=38626B): a RAW MARKDOWN string (textResult) — NO structured fields, NO machine-readable next-step. query mode returns a small JSON searchHit[] with a `fetch` directive; scope=infrastructure / briefing modes return the giant text blob. Owner: internal/tools/knowledge.go.
• env:get (p50=1888B): {service, envs[], project?} — envs dumped VERBATIM (no filtering). env:set (537B): {process, stored[], restartSkipped, nextActions(prose)}. Owner: internal/tools/env.go::projectEnvGetResponse.
• events (p50=1047B): {projectId, events[](each w/ a `hint` prose string), summary}. logs (p50=30B! mostly empty): {entries[], hasMore}. subdomain:enable (674B): {process, subdomainUrls[], nextActions(prose), warnings[]}. dev_server:* (248-688B): flat {action,hostname,running,port,healthStatus,logTail,message}. mount/scale/manage (120-666B): {process|mounts, nextActions(prose)}. browser (p50=2154B, max=29828B): {url, steps[]} replaying each command + full a11y snapshots.

ANNOTATED REAL EXAMPLE — deploy success (samples/deploy.json, 781 bytes, scenario export-buildfromgit-self-snapshot):
{"status":"DEPLOYED"            ← [decision-head: machine-readable outcome, good]
 "mode":"ssh","sourceService":"appdev","targetService":"appdev","targetServiceId":"Ebj9…","targetServiceType":"ubuntu/nodejs@22"   ← identity block
 "message":"Successfully deployed to appdev. New container replaced old — prior SSH sessions are gone."   ← prose, human-flavored
 "buildStatus":"ACTIVE","buildDuration":"58s","sshReady":true
 "nextActions":"Dev-mode dynamic runtime is idle (no start command). Start the dev server: zerops_dev_server action=start. Then run zerops_verify."   ← THE load-bearing next step, but PROSE — agent must parse the tool name+args out of a sentence (owner next_actions.go:53)
 "warnings":["run.start is empty — app will not start after deploy"]

 "workSessionState":{…progress…}}
Every fact is true and the payload is tight (781B). The single delivery weakness here is dimension 7: the one action the agent must execute is a sentence, not a {tool,action,args} object.
families.headline: On a FAILED deploy, the structured failureClassification the agent is contractually told to read FIRST is serialized LAST — physically below ~2 KB of buildLogs/runtimeLogs (byte 2594 vs byte 643 in a real 3165-byte failure) — so the one tell ZCP built for fast recovery is the least reachable block on the wire.

findings.title: failureClassification serialized last, below 2KB of logs, contradicting its own 'read FIRST' contract
findings.claim: DeployResult declares BuildLogs/RuntimeLogs/FailedPhase (struct lines 27-31) BEFORE FailureClassification (line 52). Go marshals in declaration order, so on a failed deploy the agent must scroll past the entire buildLogs[] (avg 2409B) and runtimeLogs[] (avg 1817B) array to reach the structured classification object — the exact block CLAUDE.md says 'Agents read this FIRST'. The decision-head ordering inverts the stated information contract.
findings.payload_evidence: deploy FAILURE, real transcript greenfield-node-postgres-dev-stage (3165B): parsed key order = [status, mode, …, suggestion, nextActions, buildLogs, buildLogsSource, failedPhase, failureClassification, workSessionState]; byte position buildLogs=643, failureClassification=2594 (delta 1951). Corpus: 33 failed deploys carry logs, p50=3676B max=7092B.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/ops/deploy_common.go::DeployResult (FailureClassification field at line 52, after BuildLogs/RuntimeLogs at 27/29)
findings.why_it_matters: REACHABILITY lens: a correct fact buried below the fold is not a correct tell. The classifier's category+signals (the structured diagnosis) is the least reachable thing exactly when the agent is in a recovery decision and most needs it up top; logs are fall-through depth per CLAUDE.md but are physically delivered first.
findings.proposed_direction: Reorder the struct so failureClassification (and suggestion) sit immediately after status/message and before buildLogs/runtimeLogs — make the structured diagnosis the literal head of a failed-deploy payload, logs the tail.

verdict.assessment: VERIFIED against ground truth. (1) PAYLOAD: extracted the cited deploy payload directly from the real transcript (eval/behavioral/runs/20260503-114249/greenfield-node-postgres-dev-stage/transcript.jsonl, turn 12). It is 3165B, status=BUILD_FAILED, mode=ssh. Marshaled key order = [status, mode, sourceService, targetService, targetServiceId, targetServiceType, message, monitorHint, buildStatus, buildDuration, suggestion, nextActions, buildLogs, buildLogsSource, failedPhase, failureClassification, workSessionState] — matches the claim exactly. Byte pos buildLogs=643, failureClassification=2594, delta=1951 — ALL three exact. Corpus aggregate independently reproduced: 33 failed deploys carry logs, p50=3676B, max=7092B — exact. (2) OWNER: internal/ops/deploy_common.go::DeployResult declares BuildLogs at line 27 and FailureClassification at line 52; encoding/json marshals in declaration order. The SSH failure path (internal/tools/deploy_ssh.go:260 deploySSHResponse) embeds *ops.DeployResult and only appends workSessionState last — no reordering, no hoisting of failureClassification. So the struct genuinely produces these bytes in this order. (3) DEFECT: CLAUDE.md verbatim says agents read failureClassification FIRST and buildLogs/runtimeLogs/failedPhase are fall-through depth; the payload physically delivers ~1951B of buildLogs before the structured classification object, inverting the stated contract for a linear-token LLM consumer in a recovery decision. The claim's specific WHERE (declaration-order marshaling, line 27 vs 52) and the contract location are both confirmed. ADVERSARIAL CAVEAT lowering severity: deploy_poll.go:140-142 mirrors the classifier's suggestedAction up into top-level suggestion (pos 535, before buildLogs at 643) AND nextActions — so the single most decision-relevant string (the suggested action) IS already above the fold. Only the full structured object (category + likelyCause + signals) is buried, not the actionable tell. The 'least reachable thing exactly when the agent most needs it' framing overstates: the agent's next-step string is reachable; the diagnosis metadata is buried.
verdict.corrected_claim: The full structured failureClassification OBJECT (category + signals + likelyCause) is serialized last (byte 2594), below ~1951B of buildLogs, contradicting the 'read this FIRST' contract — BUT its suggestedAction is already mirrored into top-level `suggestion` (byte 535) and `nextActions` above the fold via deploy_poll.go, so the agent's actionable next-step is reachable; only the structured diagnosis metadata (category/signals) is buried below the logs.

findings.title: knowledge scope=infrastructure ships a 36-38KB single markdown firehose with no structure
findings.claim: zerops_knowledge scope="infrastructure" concatenates FormatStackList + model + core reference into one textResult markdown blob. It returns the full validation-set (every stack/version, full YAML schema, full env-var reference) as the presentation set in a single fetch, when the agent's actual next decision needs one runtime + its managed deps.
findings.payload_evidence: knowledge, max=38626B (corpus by-type max=36584, _text component avg 12574B). 18 fetches exceed 20KB. samples/knowledge.json (8451B) shows the shape: a 'Service Stacks (live)' enum line listing ~25 runtimes + every version, then a full hello-world YAML, service cards, wiring patterns, decision hints.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/tools/knowledge.go (hasScope branch ~line 138: store.GetCore() + GetModel() + FormatStackList, returned via textResult)
findings.why_it_matters: HOW_MUCH + recommend-don't-enumerate: 'maximal info is actively harmful when the full set contains traps the agent then picks.' A 36KB blob blows context budget and forces the agent to filter the validation-set itself; correct>complete is violated.
findings.proposed_direction: Split scope into a small always-on structured 'shape' (the one runtime + its deps + the few schema rules that gate the next YAML) plus uri=-addressable deep sections the agent pulls on demand — stop shipping the whole reference per call.

verdict.assessment:
PAYLOAD: Confirmed against plans/response-audit-corpus/index.jsonl. Knowledge _text max = 38626B, by-type corpus max = 36584B, exactly 18 fetches >=20KB (values: 36584,36991,38530,38535,38626). samples/knowledge.json is 8451B (matches claim) with the exact shape claimed: 'Service Stacks (live)' enum line listing ~25 runtimes+all versions, full hello-world YAML, Service Cards, Wiring Patterns, Decision Hints, Version Check. The 36991B transcript fetch (eval/.../delivery-git-push-actions-setup) was triggered by input {"scope":"infrastructure"} — the exact input the claim names.

OWNER: Confirmed at internal/tools/knowledge.go:138-164. The hasScope branch does result=GetCore() (full themes/core.md, 26275B — import.yaml Schema, zerops.yaml Schema, Provision/Generate/Runtime Rules, env-var reference), prepends GetModel() (full themes/model.md, 9090B), prepends FormatStackList(schemaCache.Get) (every active runtime/managed stack + every concrete version), and returns ONE textResult(result). core+model+stacklist+separators ≈ 36-37KB, matching the observed 36991B. So the symbol genuinely PRODUCES this byte volume as a single markdown blob — the 'FormatStackList + model + core into one textResult' claim is literally the code.

DEFECT: Real. It is the full validation-set (every stack/version enum + complete YAML schema + full env-var reference) shipped as one unstructured blob. A narrower mechanism exists in the SAME handler (Mode 2 briefing runtime=/services= → GetBriefing, stack-specific + session-mode-filtered), so the firehose is avoidable when the next decision needs one runtime + its managed deps — validating the 'presentation-set ≠ validation-set' critique.

CAVEATS narrowing it: (1) schema doc mandates scope='infrastructure' 'before generating YAML', so it is once-per-workflow, NOT re-dumped every turn (18 of 123 knowledge fetches; rest are narrower briefing/query/recipe modes) — the 're-dump every turn' anti-pattern is mostly respected. (2) It is curated single-owner reference (core.md/model.md), not a raw schema dump, so single-source-of-truth is intact; the defect is granularity, not duplication. (3) Cited '_text avg 12574B' overstates — true all-knowledge _text avg = 10913B; not load-bearing.
verdict.corrected_claim: zerops_knowledge scope="infrastructure" returns FormatStackList + full model.md + full core.md concatenated into one ~36-38KB textResult markdown blob (max observed 38626B; 18 of 123 knowledge fetches exceed 20KB). It delivers the full validation-set (every active stack/version, complete import.yaml + zerops.yaml schema, full env-var reference) as the presentation set, with no per-decision narrowing to the agent's one runtime + its managed deps — even though the same handler offers a narrower runtime=/services= briefing mode. Caveat: it is a single mandated pre-YAML fetch (not re-dumped per turn) and is curated single-owner reference, not a raw schema dump.

findings.title: discover re-dumps the 513B adoptable-warning paragraph on every call (surface-once violation) duplicating a per-service field
findings.claim: Whenever any service has adoptionState="adoptable", discover appends a 513-byte prose paragraph instructing adoption — and re-emits it IN FULL on every subsequent discover that still has an adoptable service. The same actionable fact is already carried structurally as services[].adoptionState="adoptable" per service, so the paragraph is a re-derivable restatement, repeated up to dozens of times per run.
findings.payload_evidence: discover, samples/discover.json (1347B) warnings[0] is the full paragraph. Corpus: 704 discover rows, 91 carry the warnings component; greenfield-node-postgres-dev-stage issues 42 discover calls in one run, launch-production-from-standard-pair 34 — each adoptable-state call re-ships the same ~513B.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/tools/discover.go:132-141 (adoptCandidates → result.Warnings append)
findings.why_it_matters: surface-once principle: don't re-dump every turn. The TELL (warning paragraph) and the structured CHECK signal (adoptionState field) are two copies of one concept; the prose copy adds 513B per call with zero new information after the first emit and competes with the live service list for the agent's attention.
findings.proposed_direction: Emit the full adoption-how-to paragraph at most once per session (or only when the agent actually attempts a gated mutation); keep adoptionState as the always-present structured signal and let discover stay terse.

verdict.assessment:
PAYLOAD: Verified plans/response-audit-corpus/samples/discover.json (tool=zerops_discover, kind=discover, 1347B response). warnings[0] is the adoptable paragraph, actual size 531 bytes (claim says 513B — wrong but ballpark). services[].adoptionState="adoptable" IS carried per-service (appdev, appstage) in the same payload, so the field+prose coexist as claimed. Corpus-level numbers match EXACTLY: 704 discover rows, 91 carry the warnings component. CODE OWNER: internal/tools/discover.go:132-141 produces exactly this string via result.Warnings=append gated on len(adoptCandidates)>0 — cited owner and line range correct.

REFUTATION of the load-bearing claim ("re-emits IN FULL on every subsequent discover... repeated up to dozens of times per run"): the cited "42 discover calls in greenfield" and "34 in launch-production" are AGGREGATES ACROSS ALL SUITES in the month-long corpus, NOT per-run. Per single run, greenfield issues at most 4 discover calls; launch-production at most 4. Within a single run, at most 1 discover call carries the adoptable warning (max warnings-bearing per (suite,scenario) = 1 for both named scenarios). Across the ENTIRE corpus the maximum any single run re-emits a warnings-discover row is 2 — and several of those 2-counts are the resumable warning (a different paragraph), not the adoptable one. There is no "surface-once violation": the paragraph appears ~once per run when adoptable services exist, never "dozens" of times. The redundancy-with-field premise is also weak: the prose carries net-new actionable info absent from the adoptionState field (which mutating workflows reject with ADOPT_REQUIRED, that read-only diagnostics work pre-adopt, that zerops_verify carries the Recovery call), so it is not a pure re-derivable restatement of the boolean-ish field.
verdict.corrected_claim: The adoptable warning paragraph (~531B, not 513B) is emitted on each discover call that has an adoptable service, but in practice ~once per run (max 1 warnings-bearing adoptable discover per run across the whole corpus; absolute max 2 warnings-discover of any kind per run). It partially duplicates the per-service adoptionState="adoptable" field but adds net-new actionable guidance (which workflows gate, what read-only ops are allowed pre-adopt, the exact recovery call) not present in the field. There is no surface-once / re-dump violation. At most a low-severity stylistic note: the warning could be skippable on repeat discovers within one session, but the data shows repeats are near-zero.

findings.title: nextActions is free-text prose with inline tool calls across 7 owners; only 2 surfaces emit a structured nextCall
findings.claim: deploy/import/env/manage/subdomain all deliver their load-bearing next step as a nextActions STRING that embeds the tool name and args inside a sentence (e.g. 'Start the dev server: zerops_dev_server action=start. Then run zerops_verify.'). The agent must parse tool+action+args out of prose. A machine-readable nextCall object exists in the codebase (destructive_ack.go, launch_status_recovery.go) but is not used by the routine per-tool happy/precondition paths.
findings.payload_evidence: deploy nextActions string (next_actions.go:53); import.json nextActions='Verify services: zerops_discover. Continue workflow: mount dev, discover env vars, write code, then deploy.'; env-set.json nextActions='…Restart manually (zerops_manage action=restart) or deploy…'; subdomain-enable.json nextActions='Subdomain active. Verify: zerops_verify.' nextCall json tag found only in internal/tools/destructive_ack.go + launch_status_recovery.go.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/ops/deploy_common.go (NextActions string), internal/ops/import.go, internal/tools/env.go, internal/ops/manage.go, internal/ops/subdomain.go — all `NextActions string json:"nextActions"`
findings.why_it_matters: STRUCTURED-vs-PROSE: the one thing the agent should EXECUTE is delivered as text it must read+parse. A {tool,action,args} object would be directly executable and drift-proof; a sentence can be misread and can't be schema-checked. ZCP already proved the pattern works (nextCall) but didn't generalize it.
findings.proposed_direction: Promote nextActions to an optional structured nextCall {tool, action, args} on the per-tool responses where the next step is a single concrete call, keeping the prose only for genuinely multi-step guidance.

verdict.assessment:
PAYLOAD: All four cited payloads exist verbatim in plans/response-audit-corpus/samples/. deploy.json carries nextActions="Dev-mode dynamic runtime is idle (no start command). Start the dev server: zerops_dev_server action=start. Then run zerops_verify."; import.json="Verify services: zerops_discover. Continue workflow: mount dev, discover env vars, write code, then deploy."; env-set.json="...Restart manually (zerops_manage action=restart) or deploy to pick it up."; subdomain-enable.json="Subdomain active. Verify: zerops_verify." All five surfaces (deploy/import/env/manage/subdomain) deliver next-step ONLY via a NextActions STRING — confirmed via top_keys: no structured next-call field accompanies the prose on any routine happy-path response. The strings genuinely embed tool+action inside sentences.

CODE OWNER: Finding's attribution is partly WRONG but the substance holds. (1) Cited "internal/ops/next_actions.go:53" is actually internal/tools/next_actions.go:53 (line correct, package wrong). (2) rendering_owner claims each of deploy_common.go/import.go/env.go/manage.go/subdomain.go PRODUCES the string — reality: the prose CONTENT is centralized in internal/tools/next_actions.go (package-level constants + deploySuccessNextActions func) for deploy/import/manage/subdomain; only env-set's prose lives in env.go:293. The owner files hold the `NextActions string json:"nextActions"` struct FIELD, not the content. Wiring confirmed: deploy_poll.go:71, import.go:329/332, manage.go:56-101, subdomain.go:109.

STRUCTURED-EXISTS CLAIM: Imprecise naming but substantively true. The field literally named `nextCall` (launch_status_recovery.go:33) is itself a STRING, not an object — so "nextCall object exists" conflates two things. The genuine structured {tool,args} corrective is named RetryCall (destructive_ack.go:57-61, json tag "retryCall"), plus {tool,action,args} Recovery objects in requires_setup_input.go and workflow_checks_local_env.go. All three live on ERROR/refusal/precondition paths — matching the finding's qualifier that they are "not used by the routine per-tool happy/precondition paths." So the structured-pattern-exists-but-unused-on-routine-paths claim is correct.

DEFECT REALITY: The structural observation is real and confirmed. But the strings are short, deterministic, mostly package-level constants naming a SINGLE canonical next tool (zerops_verify / zerops_discover / zerops_dev_server). No corpus evidence of an agent misparsing them. This is a drift-proofing / structural-consistency improvement (a {tool,action,args} object can be schema-checked and is execute-ready), not an active impairment of the agent's ability to act. Hence the claimed "high" overstates impact.
verdict.corrected_claim: Routine per-tool success/precondition responses (deploy, import, env-set, manage, subdomain) deliver the load-bearing next step ONLY as a free-text `nextActions` string that embeds the tool name + action inside a sentence; no structured executable next-call accompanies them. A structured executable-call object DOES exist in the codebase (RetryCall {tool,args} in destructive_ack.go; {tool,action,args} Recovery in requires_setup_input.go / workflow_checks_local_env.go) but only on destructive-refusal / precondition-error paths — the routine happy paths were never converted. NOTE: the prose CONTENT for deploy/import/manage/subdomain is centralized in internal/tools/next_actions.go (not the per-owner files the finding names); the field named `nextCall` (launch_status_recovery.go) is itself a string, not the structured object — the real structured object is `retryCall`.

findings.title: env:get dumps the full env validation-set including platform noise instead of the app-relevant subset
findings.claim: projectEnvGetResponse returns s.Envs verbatim with no filtering. ~36% of returned keys are platform-injected machinery (PATH, appVersionId, appVersionName, serviceId, projectId, documentRoot, hostname, ZEROPS_DEBUG_BUILD, ZEROPS_DEBUG_RUNTIME_PREPARE) the agent rarely needs when its question is 'what are my wiring vars'. The validation-set is presented as the choice-set.
findings.payload_evidence: env-get.json (1888B): 25 envs returned, 9 are platform noise (PATH alone is a ~250-char string). The app-relevant set (DB_*, APP_*, zeropsSubdomain, CACHE_STORE…) is interleaved with PATH/appVersionId/etc.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/tools/env.go::projectEnvGetResponse (line 130; resp.Envs = s.Envs with no filter)
findings.why_it_matters: validation-set ≠ presentation-set: the agent is shown the firehose and must filter for the few keys it acts on. PATH/appVersionId are reference at best; surfacing them inline dilutes the wiring vars that are the actual decision input.
findings.proposed_direction: Partition env:get into the user/yaml-sourced vars (head) and a collapsed platform-injected group (or omit unless explicitly requested), so the agent sees its wiring vars first.

findings.title: failed-deploy suggestedAction is serialized three times (suggestion + nextActions + failureClassification.suggestedAction)
findings.claim: P7 correctly made suggestion, nextActions, and failureClassification.suggestedAction all DERIVE from one owner (the classifier) so they can't drift — good single-source design. The delivery side-effect is the SAME string ships three times in one failed-deploy payload, inflating bytes and giving the agent three identical prose copies of one instruction.
findings.payload_evidence: deploy_poll.go:140-142 sets result.Suggestion = result.NextActions = FailureClassification.SuggestedAction. avg components: suggestion=353B, nextActions=96B, plus suggestedAction inside the 559B failureClassification — three positions in the same response.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/tools/deploy_poll.go:140-146 (assigns the same classifier string to Suggestion and NextActions; struct also carries it inside FailureClassification)
findings.why_it_matters: surface-once within a single response: tell==check is satisfied (one owner) but the agent reads the identical recovery sentence in three places, which wastes bytes and adds no decision value — correct>complete argues for one canonical placement.
findings.proposed_direction: Keep the single owner but emit the action ONCE (inside failureClassification.suggestedAction, hoisted to the head) and drop the duplicate suggestion/nextActions copies on classified failures.

findings.title: subdomain/deploy emit subdomainUrl as live-ready while a co-located warning says it returned HTTP 502 — a half-truth at send-time
findings.claim: subdomain:enable (and deploy auto-enable) return subdomainUrls[]/subdomainAccessEnabled=true together with a warning that the same URL was NOT HTTP-ready (502) at send-time. The positive structured field reads as 'URL live' while the live platform state at send-time was 'route enabled but not yet serving'. The agent reading the structured field first may act on a not-yet-live URL.
findings.payload_evidence: subdomain-enable.json (674B): subdomainUrls=['https://appdev-2445.prg1.zerops.app'], nextActions='Subdomain active. Verify: zerops_verify.' AND warnings=['…not HTTP-ready… HTTP 502 (agent may need to retry verify)']. deploy.json similarly sets subdomainAccessEnabled=true.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/tools/subdomain.go (subdomainUrls + nextActions 'Subdomain active'); internal/tools/deploy_subdomain.go (maybeAutoEnableSubdomain sets SubdomainAccessEnabled/SubdomainURL)
findings.why_it_matters: LIVE-TRUTH lens: a boolean that reflects 'route configured' presented as 'active/live' when the live probe at send-time was 502 is a stored-intent proxy, not live truth. nextActions saying 'Subdomain active' contradicts the warning in the same payload.
findings.proposed_direction: Make subdomainAccessEnabled/nextActions reflect the actual HTTP-readiness probe result at send-time (enabled-but-not-ready is a distinct state), so the structured field and the warning agree.

findings.title: browser replays every command + full a11y snapshot, ballooning to ~30KB; only the final state is decision-relevant
findings.claim: zerops_browser returns a steps[] array echoing every command, its success bool, result, and a FULL accessibility snapshot after snapshot commands. Multi-step interactions re-emit the entire ref tree per snapshot, so the response grows to tens of KB while the agent's next decision usually needs only the final page state + any errors.
findings.payload_evidence: browser, p50=2154B but max=29828B (samples/browser.json shows steps[] replaying open/click/snapshot/fill/click/wait/snapshot, each snapshot embedding the full refs map + snapshot text).
findings.rendering_owner: internal/tools/browser*.go (steps[] component, avg 4063B; consoleOutput/errorsOutput small)
findings.why_it_matters: HOW_MUCH: the signal (did the interaction succeed, what is the page now, what errored) is a fraction of the bytes; re-emitting every intermediate snapshot is reference the agent re-derives, and a 30KB payload competes hard for context budget.
findings.proposed_direction: Return the final snapshot + a compact per-step success/error ledger by default; gate full intermediate snapshots behind an explicit verbose flag.

findings.title: logs returns an effectively empty body (30B) on the common no-match case with no guidance
findings.claim: logs p50 is 30 bytes — {"entries":[],"hasMore":false}. On the very common empty-result case the agent gets a bare empty array with no nextActions and no hint about widening the time window / severity, unlike every other per-tool response which carries nextActions.
findings.payload_evidence: logs, samples/logs.json = {"entries":[],"hasMore":false} (30B); by-type p50=30 max=3983 — the distribution is bimodal (empty vs a real 1KB+ entries dump).
findings.rendering_owner: internal/platform/logfetcher.go::FetchLogs (entries+hasMore; no nextActions field on the logs response)
findings.why_it_matters: WHAT/right-info: an empty result is itself a decision point (widen window? wrong severity? service not logging?) and the per-tool family otherwise always hands the agent a next step; logs alone leaves it to infer.
findings.proposed_direction: When entries is empty, attach a short nextActions hint (widen since=, drop severity filter, or check the service is running) so the empty case is actionable like the rest of the family.

findings.title: knowledge scope ignores its own scopeLoaded tracker — re-ships the 36KB firehose on every repeat call
findings.claim: KnowledgeTracker.RecordScope() sets scopeLoaded=true, but the knowledge handler's hasScope branch never consults it to short-circuit a repeat fetch; it rebuilds and returns the full reference each time scope=infrastructure is called. The tracker is a workflow-side hint, not a tool-side dedup, so within a run the firehose can be re-delivered multiple times.
findings.payload_evidence: Corpus: delivery-git-push-actions-setup issues 3 knowledge fetches >20KB in one run; greenfield-fullstack-multi-runtime 4 big fetches. knowledge_tracker.go records scopeLoaded but knowledge.go hasScope branch (returns textResult(result)) has no scopeLoaded guard.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/tools/knowledge.go (hasScope branch calls tracker.RecordScope() but does not read kt.scopeLoaded); internal/ops/knowledge_tracker.go::RecordScope
