findings.why_it_matters: surface-once: the heaviest single payload in the family can be re-delivered whole; the dedup signal exists but is not wired to suppress the repeat, so a re-fetch costs the full 36KB again.
findings.proposed_direction: On repeat scope=infrastructure within a session, return a terse 'reference already loaded (see prior fetch)' pointer instead of the full blob, or have the handler honor scopeLoaded.

families.anatomy:
This is a cross-cutting lens, so the "per-response-type content map" is about which COMPONENTS recur ACROSS kinds, and which OWNER re-emits each. Three recurring component classes dominate:

(1) STACK CATALOG (the live service-version list). Two distinct Go owners render the SAME underlying data (`internal/knowledge/versions_format.go::buildCatalogView` → `catalogLines`): `FormatStackList` (compact, header "## Available Service Stacks (live, active concrete versions)", 1214 bytes) is injected as the `availableStacks` field by `tools/workflow_bootstrap.go::populateStacks` on bootstrap-start responses; `FormatServiceStacks` (rich, header "## Service Stacks (live)", [B] markers) is prepended by `knowledge/briefing.go::GetBriefing` to EVERY `zerops_knowledge` response (~1044-byte prefix before the actual answer). At bootstrap-discover the agent calls both tools in adjacent turns and receives the same catalog twice from two owners.

(2) WORK-SESSION-STATE (the lifecycle annotation `workSessionState`). One owner — `tools/deploy_local.go::sessionAnnotations` (+ `attachWorkSessionState`) — re-attaches it to EVERY deploy/verify/close-mode/git-push/build-integration response. It is DERIVED live per call (`DeriveCloseState` + `AutoCloseProgressOf`), so its `progress` sub-object is legitimately fresh truth; its `note`/`reason` prose is the only verbatim-repeating part.

(3) SYNTHESIZED GUIDANCE PROSE (the develop/status markdown monolith). `internal/workflow/render.go::RenderStatus` concatenates the full `[]Guidance` atom list — produced by `synthesize.go::Synthesize` — into one `_text` blob. `Synthesize` dedupes (atomID+body) WITHIN one response but has NO cross-turn memory, and `RenderStatus` is re-run on every `develop:start`/`status` call, so the entire 15-32 KB manual re-ships when the agent re-enters develop or recovers via status.

ANNOTATED REAL EXAMPLE — `workflow:develop:start::prose` (kind), 15599 bytes (sample `workflow-develop-start-prose.json`), `top_keys: []` (pure `_text` markdown, NO machine-readable field). Block layout, in send order: "## Status" header (~40 B) → Phase line + Services block + "Auto-close blocked… Next: zerops_deploy targetService=\"app\"" (the live decision, ~500 B) → then ~14 KB of "Guidance:" atoms: first-deploy-branch, "Where values come from", self-shadow, env catalog, scaffold-zerops-yaml (with full YAML skeleton), HTTP diagnostics, static-runtime-workflow (with a SECOND full YAML skeleton), self-deploy-destruction-risk, knowledge-on-demand, work-session-auto-close, run-first-deploy, per-service-verify-matrix → finally "Next:\n  ▸ Primary: Deploy app — zerops_deploy targetService=\"app\"" at the very BOTTOM. The single load-bearing instruction (deploy app) is rendered once near the top inside the Services block and once at the very end, with ~14 KB of reference manual wrapped around it and no structured nextCall object anywhere.
families.headline: The same content is re-handed to the agent turn after turn — most acutely the 15-32 KB develop/status guidance monolith (re-synthesized whole on every status/re-entry, delivered 2-6× in 14 transcripts) and the live stack catalog rendered by two separate owners into two adjacent responses — because guidance is assembled fresh per call with no cross-turn surface-once memory and the catalog has one data owner but two presenters.

findings.title: The 15-32 KB develop/status guidance monolith is re-synthesized whole on every re-entry — no cross-turn surface-once memory
findings.claim: RenderStatus concatenates the entire synthesized atom list into one _text blob and is re-run on every develop:start and status call. Synthesize dedupes (atomID,body) only WITHIN a single response; it carries no record of what the agent already received earlier in the session. So an agent that re-enters develop or recovers via action=status is re-handed the full manual it already has. Measured in the corpus: develop:start::prose alone is delivered 2× in 12 transcripts and 3× in 2; combined with status::prose it reaches 6× in one transcript (~90-180 KB of near-identical guidance to one agent).
findings.payload_evidence: kind workflow:develop:start::prose, 15599 bytes (avg 23070, max 32252); top_keys:[] (pure _text). Verbatim tail after ~15 KB of atoms: "Next:\n  ▸ Primary: Deploy app — zerops_deploy targetService=\"app\"". Per-transcript distribution (index.jsonl): develop-prose+status-prose = 2x in 20 transcripts, 3x in 3, 6x in 1.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/workflow/render.go:RenderStatus (concatenates resp.Guidance) fed by internal/workflow/synthesize.go:Synthesize (seen-map dedup is per-call only, line ~114)
findings.why_it_matters: Violates surface-once: 'a correct fact buried below the fold is not a correct tell, and re-dumping every turn' is the named failure. Re-shipping a 23 KB manual the agent already parsed burns context window, buries the one fresh next-action, and on a 6× transcript wastes >150 KB. The dedup primitive already exists intra-response; it just has no session scope.
findings.proposed_direction: Give Synthesize/RenderStatus a per-session 'already-delivered atom' ledger so re-entry/status responses emit only the live decision-head (Phase/Services/Next) plus atoms NEW since last delivery, replacing repeats with a one-line 'guidance unchanged — see prior' pointer.

verdict.assessment: PAYLOAD verified against plans/response-audit-corpus/index.jsonl. workflow:develop:start::prose appears 265×, avg=23070 / max=32252 bytes (matches claim exactly), all top_keys:[] pure _text, the cited 15599-byte entry exists, and the verbatim tail 'Primary: Deploy app — zerops_deploy targetService="app"' exists in the source transcript (20260604-212612/greenfield-website-from-brief). Per-transcript multiplicity verified: develop-prose alone = 2× in 12 transcripts, 3× in 2 (exact match); develop+status combined = 2× in 21, 3× in 3, 6× in 1 (claim said 20 vs actual 21 — trivial off-by-one; 3× and 6× exact). CODE OWNER confirmed: render.go:26 RenderStatus → renderGuidance (line 354) dumps every synthesized atom body into one Guidance section. synthesize.go:60 Synthesize creates seen:=make(map[string]struct{},len(pendings)) at line 114 (exact line claimed) — a fresh per-call local map; its own comment scopes dedup to one render set, zero session persistence. DEFECT REAL: the 6× transcript re-synthesizes the ~21 KB first-deploy manual 3 times (turns 9/21/31, within ~100 bytes of each other; the 'develop first-deploy branch' signature recurs 6×) — confirmed near-identical re-ship, only the live state header differs. Genuinely burns context and re-buries the fresh next-action; no existing session-scope mitigation. ONE OVERSTATEMENT: the claimed '~90-180 KB / >150 KB wasted on the 6× transcript' conflates the 23 KB develop-prose with status-prose. status::prose averages 6.5 KB (min 2.3 KB) — the 6× = 3 develop-prose (~21 KB) + 3 status-prose (~2.5 KB), ~72 KB total, not 150 KB; redundant develop-monolith portion ~64 KB. Worst case is roughly half the claimed magnitude, but the core defect (no cross-turn surface-once memory; whole monolith re-synthesized on every re-entry) is fully substantiated.
verdict.corrected_claim: Defect holds as stated except the worst-case waste figure. Correction: status::prose is a SMALL payload (avg 6.5 KB, min 2.3 KB), not part of the 23 KB monolith — only develop:start::prose is the 23 KB/max-32 KB manual. The 6× transcript wastes ~72 KB total (3× ~21 KB develop-monolith ≈ 64 KB genuine redundancy + 3× ~2.5 KB status), not >150 KB. Re-state as: 'the 23 KB develop first-deploy monolith is re-synthesized and re-delivered up to 3× per session with no cross-turn memory; one agent receives the develop-monolith ~64 KB redundantly across a session.'

findings.title: The live stack catalog is rendered by two owners into two adjacent responses (availableStacks + knowledge prefix)
findings.claim: One data owner (knowledge/versions_format.go::buildCatalogView) is presented by TWO formatters into TWO different response surfaces. FormatStackList becomes the bootstrap availableStacks field (1214 B); FormatServiceStacks is unconditionally prepended to EVERY zerops_knowledge response (~1044 B before the actual answer, even for a PHP-recipe query whose input has nothing to do with stack selection). At bootstrap-discover the agent calls zerops_workflow start (gets availableStacks) and zerops_knowledge (gets ## Service Stacks (live)) in adjacent turns and receives the same catalog twice from two independent producers that don't know about each other.
findings.payload_evidence: knowledge.json (8451 B) opens verbatim '## Service Stacks (live)\n[B]=also usable as build.base…' then the real content '# PHP Hello world on Zerops' starts at byte ~1044; input={} . bootstrap-classic-start-session-active.json carries availableStacks (1214 B) '## Available Service Stacks (live, active concrete versions)…' in the same discover phase. 183 knowledge responses in corpus, all lead with the catalog.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/knowledge/versions_format.go:FormatStackList + FormatServiceStacks (both call catalogLines over the same catalogView); injected by internal/tools/workflow_bootstrap.go:populateStacks and internal/knowledge/briefing.go:GetBriefing (line 37)
findings.why_it_matters: Two presenters of one owner is the tell-tell duplication the info-contract warns against: the agent gets the validation-set twice in one decision window. The knowledge prefix is unconditional, so it is pure wrong-time noise whenever the query isn't about choosing a stack.
findings.proposed_direction: Make the knowledge briefing's stack-catalog prefix conditional (emit only for stack/version queries), and when a bootstrap response already carries availableStacks in the same session-phase, suppress the duplicate prefix or have one surface point at the other.

verdict.assessment:
PAYLOAD: knowledge.json verified — opens verbatim '## Service Stacks (live)
[B]=also usable as build.base in zerops.yaml

' then real content '# PHP Hello world on Zerops' at byte 1078 (claim ~1044 = char count; utf-8 byte count 1078); total 8451 B. availableStacks: session-active sample = 1206 B leading '## Available Service Stacks (live, active concrete versions)' (claim 1214 B ~matches; the start-obj sample is an older 722 B variant = the index's 729 figure). 183 knowledge responses confirmed. CODE OWNER: buildCatalogView (catalog_view.go:80) is the genuine SINGLE owner; both FormatStackList (versions_format.go:12) and FormatServiceStacks (:33) call it. FormatStackList -> availableStacks via workflow_bootstrap.go:295; FormatServiceStacks -> briefing prefix via briefing.go:37. So the shared-owner / two-surface structure is real, and the two surfaces co-occur in 60 corpus transcripts.

REFUTATION of the load-bearing premise: the claim states FormatServiceStacks is 'unconditionally prepended to EVERY zerops_knowledge response... even for a PHP-recipe query whose input has nothing to do with stack selection.' This is FALSE. FormatServiceStacks is reached ONLY from GetBriefing (Mode 3, runtime=/services= input). Query (Mode 2), recipe (Mode 4), and fetch (Mode 5) return textResult/jsonResult with NO catalog. Empirical corpus tally across all 183 calls: catalog leads 61/61 briefing, 0/19 recipe, 0/59 query, 0/26 fetch (scope Mode 1 uses the DIFFERENT compact FormatStackList: 16/18). The cited 8451-B payload's REAL input (from transcript 20260605-042316) is {"runtime":"php-nginx@8.5","services":["mariadb@10.6"]} — a BRIEFING call, i.e. precisely a stack-selection decision window, not 'a PHP-recipe query.' The 'recipe query' example the claim invokes as the wrong-time case is the exact mode (recipe AND query both = 0) that carries NO prefix. The 'why-it-matters' ('pure wrong-time noise whenever the query isn't about choosing a stack') therefore collapses: the prefix appears only when the agent IS choosing a stack. The claim is also internally self-contradictory — it calls them 'two independent producers that don't know about each other' while also (correctly) naming the single shared owner buildCatalogView. The input={} in the index is a corpus-extraction artifact (all 183 record {} regardless of real args; byte sizes 410..36991 prove varied modes), so the claim's 'input={}' evidence does not support 'unconditional.'
verdict.corrected_claim: A single owner (knowledge/catalog_view.go::buildCatalogView) is rendered by two formatters into two surfaces: FormatStackList -> bootstrap availableStacks (~1206 B) and FormatServiceStacks -> a prefix on zerops_knowledge BRIEFING responses (Mode 3, runtime/services input; ~1078 B before content). Both are stack-selection / YAML-authoring contexts, and they co-occur in ~60 corpus sessions, so an agent can receive overlapping (not byte-identical: compact vs rich [B]-marked) catalog data twice in one bootstrap session. The prefix is NOT on query/recipe/fetch responses, so there is no wrong-time-noise problem; the residual concern is intra-session overlap between availableStacks and the briefing prefix, which is low-impact stylistic redundancy from one consistent owner, not a drift defect.

findings.title: develop/status responses ship as a single markdown _text blob with no machine-readable nextCall
findings.claim: Across the whole develop/status family the response is delivered as one prose string (top_keys:[] for develop:start::prose; _text-only for status::prose), with the next action expressed only as a prose line ('▸ Primary: Deploy app — zerops_deploy targetService="app"') the agent must parse out of ~15 KB. There is no typed nextCall/nextActions object the agent can execute directly, unlike the terse mutation responses (deploy.json carries a structured nextActions string; verify carries structured checks). The decision-critical instruction is the same in every render but the agent re-parses it from prose each time.
findings.payload_evidence: workflow-develop-start-prose.json bytes=15599 top_keys=[] — entire payload is _text. workflow-status-prose.json (7112 B) _text-only. Contrast: deploy.json has typed nextActions; verify.json has typed checks/workSessionState. by-type.md: develop:start::prose avg component _text=16520, status::prose _text=6528.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/workflow/render.go:RenderStatus → renderPlan (emits the plan as the trailing 'Next:' prose section rather than a structured field); textResult() wrapping in tools/workflow_develop.go:renderDevelopBriefing
findings.why_it_matters: Reachability + structured-vs-prose: the load-bearing next-action sits at the bottom after ~15 KB and is prose, not an executable field. An LLM must scan the whole manual to find what to do, and there is no typed object to act on — maximizing parse cost and the chance the agent acts on a buried mid-document instruction instead.
findings.proposed_direction: Lift the next-action into a top-level structured nextCall {tool,args} field at the HEAD of the response (alongside the prose), so the agent executes the field and reads the manual only on demand.

verdict.assessment:
PAYLOAD (confirmed): workflow-develop-start-prose.json bytes=15599 top_keys=[] — entire payload is one _text string (response_text 15459 chars); workflow-status-prose.json bytes=7112 top_keys=[] _text-only. by-type.md averages match exactly (develop:start::prose _text=16520, status::prose _text=6528). Contrast confirmed: deploy.json carries top-level keys incl. nextActions + workSessionState; verify.json carries a typed checks list ([{name,status}]) + workSessionState. So the structural delta (prose blob vs structured fields) is real.

RENDERING OWNER (confirmed exactly as cited): internal/workflow/render.go:RenderStatus(26)→renderPlan(385) emits the next-action ONLY as the trailing 'Next: ▸ Primary: …' prose section; internal/tools/workflow_develop.go:293 calls textResult(workflow.RenderStatus(...)) with second return nil; textResult (convert.go:114) wraps ONLY TextContent. Decisively, BuildPlan produces a fully typed, executable workflow.Plan{Primary NextAction{Tool,Args,Label,Rationale}} with JSON tags — it EXISTS in code, is built every render, then flattened to prose and discarded. So 'there is no typed nextCall the agent can execute' is true on the wire despite a ready typed object existing internally.

DEFECT REALITY — the structural core holds, the 'buried' rhetoric does NOT. For the flagship develop:start payload the decision-critical action zerops_deploy targetService=\"app\" appears TWICE: at offset 567 (4% through, in the envelope's early 'Next:' blocker line) AND at offset 15403 (100%, the plan render). It is therefore NOT only at the bottom and the agent is NOT forced to scan ~15 KB to find it — that part of the claim is refuted. The bottom-only positioning holds only for status-prose (Next:@98%) and bootstrap-status (@96%), which lack the early duplicate. The prose is deterministic ('same in every render'), so the parse cost is stable rather than nondeterministic.
verdict.corrected_claim: Develop/status responses ship as a single markdown _text blob (top_keys:[]) with the next action expressed only as a prose 'Next: ▸ Primary:' line — there is no typed nextCall/nextActions field on the wire, even though a fully-typed executable workflow.Plan{Primary NextAction{Tool,Args}} is built internally (workflow_develop.go:293 → RenderStatus → renderPlan) and then flattened to prose and discarded. Unlike deploy (top-level nextActions key) and verify (typed checks list), the agent has no structured object to act on and must extract the tool+args from prose. NARROWING: the action is NOT buried-only-at-the-bottom for develop:start — it is duplicated near the top (offset ~4%, in the envelope's 'Next:' blocker line) as well as at 100%, so the '~15 KB to find it' framing only applies to status/bootstrap-status prose, which surface it once at ~96-98%.

findings.title: Full 1214-byte stack catalog attached at adopt/recipe bootstrap-start, where the agent chooses no stack
findings.claim: needsStacks() gates the catalog to the discover step generically (resp.Current.Name == discover), but does NOT distinguish route. The bootstrap session-start IS at the discover step for all routes, so adopt and recipe sessions still receive the full 1214-byte version menu — even though the adopt guidance explicitly says the agent only names existing hostnames in scope (the plan is derived) and the recipe route derives types from the recipe's import YAML. Presenting the whole validation-set as a choice-menu where there is no type choice to make.
findings.payload_evidence: workflow-bootstrap-adopt-start-session-active.json (5263 B) carries availableStacks=1214 while its detailedGuide says 'scope is just the hostname list; the plan is derived for you'. Recent split (suite>=20260604): availableStacks on bootstrap/adopt:start x34, bootstrap/recipe:start x18 — all 1214 B.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/tools/workflow_bootstrap.go:needsStacks (returns true for any discover-step response regardless of route) / populateStacks
findings.why_it_matters: Recommend-don't-enumerate: the catalog informs a CLASSIC type decision; for adopt (names existing) and recipe (derives) there is no such decision, so the menu is a firehose with no consumer — the same wrong-time-noise the needsStacks doc-comment was written to kill for completed responses.
findings.proposed_direction: Make needsStacks route-aware: attach availableStacks only on route=classic discover responses; adopt/recipe omit it (their plan derivation already owns the types).

findings.title: Next-action precedes ~14 KB of guidance only by being duplicated; the canonical 'Next:' is last
findings.claim: RenderStatus's fixed section order is Phase → Services → Progress/Blockers → Guidance → Plan(Next). The Blockers line surfaces a short call-to-action above Guidance (by design), but the canonical structured Next section renders AFTER the full Guidance block. In develop:start::prose the deploy instruction reaches the agent first only because it is incidentally embedded in the Services/Blockers line ('Next: zerops_deploy targetService="app"'); the authoritative 'Next: ▸ Primary' is ~15 KB later. The two copies can and do drift in phrasing within one response.
findings.payload_evidence: workflow-develop-start-prose.json: early copy '→ Auto-close blocked: 0/1 ready… Next: zerops_deploy targetService=\"app\"'; trailing copy 'Next:\n  ▸ Primary: Deploy app — zerops_deploy targetService=\"app\"' separated by the entire Guidance block.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/workflow/render.go:RenderStatus (renderProgressAndBlockers before renderGuidance; renderPlan after)
findings.why_it_matters: Reachability: relying on a Blockers-line incidental mention to keep the action above the fold is fragile — when blockers are empty (post-close-mode, scope green) the agent must scroll past all guidance to reach the only Next. Same instruction rendered twice is also a mini-redundancy with drift surface.
findings.proposed_direction: Render the structured Plan/Next block immediately after the Services/Blockers head and before the (large) Guidance, so the action is always above the fold and stated once.

findings.title: Residual availableStacks leak on status::session-active after the surface-once fix
findings.claim: The recent (post-consolidation) data shows the availableStacks surface-once fix largely landed — old responses re-attached the catalog on complete:close (147x) and complete:provision (83x), recent responses do not. But one residual leak remains: workflow:?:status::session-active still carries availableStacks (1 recent occurrence), because needsStacks fires whenever a status/resume/iterate response happens to land on the discover step. A status recovery at discover re-ships the 1214-byte catalog the agent already saw at start.
findings.payload_evidence: Recent (suite>=20260604) availableStacks by kind: bootstrap/adopt:start x34, bootstrap/classic:start x25, bootstrap/recipe:start x18, workflow:?:status::session-active x1 (all 1214 B). Old era: complete:close x147, complete:provision x83 at 729 B (now fixed).
findings.rendering_owner: internal/tools/workflow_bootstrap.go:bootstrapStatusResult → needsStacks/populateStacks (status path re-attaches when Current.Name==discover)
findings.why_it_matters: Minor surface-once residue: status is the compaction-recovery primitive, so re-shipping the catalog there is the exact 'already-made choice re-dumped' the needsStacks comment targets — just on the status path the fix didn't fully cover.
findings.proposed_direction: Suppress availableStacks on status/resume/iterate responses (recovery surfaces) even at the discover step; the catalog belongs only on the forward-progress start/complete decision point.

findings.title: workSessionState re-sent every mutation is justified live truth, but its gated 'reason' prose repeats verbatim
findings.claim: workSessionState is attached to every deploy/verify/close-mode/git-push/build-integration response by a single owner and is DERIVED live each call (DeriveCloseState + AutoCloseProgressOf), so re-sending it is correct live-truth, not a stale snapshot — this is the right pattern. The only redundancy is the prose 'reason'/'note' (e.g. the auto-close-gated sentence) which is byte-identical across consecutive gated responses; the structured progress sub-object legitimately changes.
findings.payload_evidence: verify.json workSessionState.progress.reason: 'auto-close gated by close-mode: apidev, apistage, appdev, appstage. Set close-mode via zerops_workflow action=\"close-mode\"…' — re-emitted verbatim on each gated verify. Measured: workSessionState present in 10 distinct tool-results in one greenfield transcript.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/tools/deploy_local.go:sessionAnnotations + attachWorkSessionState (note/reason strings) ; reason from workflow.AutoCloseProgressOf
findings.why_it_matters: Timing/live-truth: this is the COUNTER-example — the field is correctly recomputed, so it is NOT a stale-bool bug. Flagged only because the repeating prose note is pure restatement; the structured fields carry the signal.
findings.proposed_direction: Keep the live structured progress on every response; drop the repeated prose note once the agent has seen the gate (emit the human note only on the first gated response or on status), relying on the structured autoCloseStatus thereafter.

findings.title: Atoms hard-code stack versions (nodejs@22, postgresql@18) whose authoritative source is the live catalog
findings.claim: Five atoms (bootstrap-classic-plan-dynamic, develop-first-deploy-scaffold-yaml, develop-static-workflow, idle-adopt-entry, scaffold-zerops-yaml) embed concrete versioned values like nodejs@22 / postgresql@18 / go@1 as inline examples, while the authoritative owner for which versions are ACTIVE is the schema-derived availableStacks catalog. These are framed as illustrative examples ('e.g. nodejs@22', 'use nodejs@22 as the convention'), so they are not yet a hard tell==check break — but they are sourced values re-authored in prose that will drift when the active-version set changes (e.g. nodejs@22 ceasing to be latest).
findings.payload_evidence: develop-start-prose 'Counter-intuitive build.base… Use nodejs@22 as the convention even when there is no JS to build'; the live catalog in the SAME corpus lists nodejs@24 (latest) · 22 · 20 — the hard-coded example is already not-latest. grep: 5 atoms under internal/content/atoms/ contain nodejs@22|postgresql@18|go@1.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/content/atoms/{develop-static-workflow,scaffold-zerops-yaml,develop-first-deploy-scaffold-yaml,...}.md (hand-authored) vs owner internal/knowledge/versions_format.go:buildCatalogView
findings.why_it_matters: Info-contract single-owner: a sourced value (active version) hand-copied into the curated tell drifts from the catalog owner; the lens flags it as latent tell==check drift even though current framing as 'example' keeps it correct-enough today.
findings.proposed_direction: Keep version mentions in atoms strictly as un-versioned placeholders or '<latest dynamic runtime>' and let the live catalog be the only place a concrete version appears, so the example can never contradict the active set.

families.anatomy:
CROSS-CUT MAP — the structured-vs-prose POLICY across all 93 response-kinds. There is NO single delivery policy: ZCP ships the agent's "what to call next" in FOUR mutually-inconsistent shapes, chosen per-handler with no shared owner.

(A) STRUCTURED-EXECUTABLE — `nextCalls[]` array of `{tool, args:{...}}` the agent passes verbatim. Found in exactly ONE kind: `workflow:bootstrap:discover::route-menu` (and `workflow:bootstrap:start::route-menu`). The agent reads `nextCalls[i]` and fires it.
(B) STRUCTURED-STRING — `nextCall` is a single ready-to-paste command STRING (not args-decomposed, but copy-paste-exact). Found in launch-active recovery (`workflow:?:status::launch-active`, `workflow:launch-production:status::launch-active`). Owner: tools/launch_status_recovery.go:74.
(C) PROSE-STRING `nextActions`/`nextStep`/`nextSteps` — a free-text sentence with the tool name + args buried INSIDE prose ("Start the dev server: zerops_dev_server action=start. Then run zerops_verify."). This is the DOMINANT mutation shape: `deploy` (474), `import` (280), `env:set` (47), `subdomain:enable` (21), `scale` (6), `manage:*`, plus export's `nextSteps[]` (string array) and git-push-setup's `nextStep`. Owner: ops/deploy_common.go:25/72 `NextActions string`, tools/next_actions.go (const prose), tools/workflow_export.go:339/371 (nextSteps string slice).
(D) PROSE-ONLY MARKDOWN — whole response is one `_text` markdown blob (`## Status … Next:`), the next-action rendered as a markdown line at the BOTTOM after all guidance. Kinds: `workflow:develop:start::prose` (265 inst, p50=15.6KB, max=23KB), `workflow:?:status::prose` (41, 7.1KB), `workflow:launch-production:status::prose` (7.1KB), `workflow:bootstrap:status::prose` (5.4KB). Owner: internal/workflow/render.go:RenderStatus → tools/convert.go:textResult, called from tools/workflow.go:1094 (handleLifecycleStatus) and tools/workflow_develop.go:293.

The cruel irony: the typed `Plan{Primary NextAction{Label,Tool,Args map[string]string,Rationale}}` struct (internal/workflow/plan.go:19-32) is FULLY machine-readable with JSON tags — but on the develop/status paths it is built by BuildPlan(), then immediately FLATTENED to a markdown `Next:\n  ▸ Primary: Deploy app — zerops_deploy targetService="app"` string by renderPlan (render.go:385) and shipped as `textResult`. The structure is computed and then thrown away.

ANNOTATED REAL EXAMPLE — `workflow:develop:start::prose`, 15599 bytes (samples/workflow-develop-start-prose.json), a SINGLE markdown `_text` blob:
  • bytes 0–600: `## Status` header + `Phase:` line + per-service line + `→ Auto-close blocked: 0/1 ready … Next: zerops_deploy targetService="app" (un-deployed edits revert…)` — the ONE blocker hint (good: near top).
  • bytes 600–15200: `Guidance:` — ~14.5KB of atom bodies (first-deploy branch, env-var channels, self-shadow, deploy-modes, HTTP-diagnostics matrix, static-runtime walkthrough, self-deploy-destruction, knowledge-on-demand, auto-close). Pure reference prose.
  • bytes ~15200–15599: `Next:\n  ▸ Primary: Deploy app — zerops_deploy targetService="app"` — the load-bearing next-call, rendered as a markdown bullet at the very BOTTOM, ~15KB below the fold. This same `{Tool:"zerops_deploy", Args:{targetService:"app"}}` existed as a typed NextAction one function-call earlier and was stringified away.
Net: the agent must parse 15.6KB of markdown to extract a single tool call that the server already held as a typed object.
families.headline: ZCP holds the agent's next action as a typed `Plan{Primary.Tool, Args}` object but ships it four incompatible ways — and on the two highest-volume guidance paths (develop:start 265×@15.6KB, status 41×@7.1KB) it flattens that object into a markdown `Next:` bullet buried below ~15KB of prose, forcing the LLM to parse instead of execute.

findings.title: develop:start ships a 15.6KB markdown blob with the next-call buried at the bottom; the typed Plan is flattened away
findings.claim: `workflow:develop:start::prose` (265 instances, p50=15.6KB, max=23KB) is delivered as ONE `_text` markdown string. The single load-bearing next-action is rendered as a `Next:\n  ▸ Primary: Deploy app — zerops_deploy targetService="app"` markdown bullet at the very END, after ~14.5KB of guidance prose. The server computed this as a typed `Plan.Primary NextAction{Tool:"zerops_deploy", Args:{"targetService":"app"}}` (plan.go:27) one call earlier, then discarded the structure via renderPlan→textResult. The agent must regex a tool call out of markdown instead of executing a JSON object.
findings.payload_evidence: workflow:develop:start::prose, 15599 bytes, samples/workflow-develop-start-prose.json: tail `Next:\n  ▸ Primary: Deploy app — zerops_deploy targetService="app"` sits ~15000 bytes after the `## Status` head; top_keys is empty (pure _text).
findings.rendering_owner: internal/workflow/render.go:RenderStatus + renderPlan (line 385-429); flattened to text at internal/tools/convert.go:textResult; called from internal/tools/workflow_develop.go:293. Typed source: internal/workflow/plan.go:19-32 (Plan/NextAction).
findings.why_it_matters: REACHABILITY: a correct next-call below 15KB of prose is not a reachable tell. The agent receives a typed object's worth of certainty re-encoded as prose it must parse — the opposite of recommend-don't-enumerate. Every develop turn pays this tax; flow-evals repeatedly show agents re-deriving the deploy call.
findings.proposed_direction: Make develop/status responses a structured envelope: top-level {status, nextCall:{tool,args}, head} from the existing Plan struct; demote the 14.5KB guidance to an optional `detail`/`guidance` field the agent reads only on ambiguity.

verdict.assessment:
Payload + code both inspected against the real corpus.

CONFIRMED facts: (1) Component `workflow:develop:start::prose` exists in plans/response-audit-corpus/index.jsonl with exactly 265 instances, all pure `_text` (top_keys empty). (2) Sample plans/response-audit-corpus/samples/workflow-develop-start-prose.json exists, is 15599 bytes, and its tail is verbatim the cited `Next:\n  ▸ Primary: Deploy app — zerops_deploy targetService="app"`. (3) Code owners are accurate: internal/workflow/render.go RenderStatus(26)→renderPlan(385) emits the bottom `Next:`/`▸ Primary:`; internal/tools/convert.go textResult(114) flattens to one `_text` string; called from internal/tools/workflow_develop.go:293 after BuildPlan(292); typed Plan/NextAction live in internal/workflow/plan.go:19-32. It IS delivered as one flat markdown blob.

REFUTED — the load-bearing 'buried' mechanism is false: the next-action `zerops_deploy targetService="app"` occurs 4 times in the payload, FIRST at char 573 (~570 bytes from the `## Status` head), inside the envelope's `→ Auto-close blocked: 0/1 ready, pending app. Next: zerops_deploy targetService="app"` line. That line is produced by blockerNextAction (render.go:245) via renderProgressAndBlockers (render.go:138), which runs at the TOP of RenderStatus (line 32) — BEFORE guidance and before renderPlan. So the single load-bearing next-call is surfaced up front, NOT 'at the very END after ~14.5KB of prose.' The bottom occurrence (char 15425) is a redundant restatement. The agent does not have to regex 14.5KB of markdown to find the call; it is in the first ~600 bytes.

ALSO WRONG: claimed p50=15.6KB / max=23KB; actual p50=25098 bytes (~25KB), max=32252 (~32KB), mean=23070. The 15599-byte sample is below the real p50, not at it. And 'typed Plan flattened away / structure discarded' is misleading — the Plan IS rendered (renderPlan), and the next-call is independently surfaced from the envelope blocker logic regardless of the Plan.

The genuine residue: the response is one undifferentiated ~25KB `_text` markdown string with no machine-parsable next-action object (no JSON top_keys). That is a real STRUCTURED_PROSE observation about delivery format and verbosity. But the finding's stated harm — REACHABILITY ('a correct next-call below 15KB of prose is not a reachable tell', 'agent must regex it out') — does not survive: the tell sits at byte ~573. The 'critical' framing rests on a false premise about WHERE the instruction is.
verdict.corrected_claim: workflow:develop:start ships as ONE flat ~25KB `_text` markdown string (p50≈25KB, max≈32KB; 265 instances) with no machine-parsable next-action object. The next-call is NOT buried: the same `zerops_deploy targetService="app"` appears at byte ~573 in the envelope's top `Next:` blocker line (render.go blockerNextAction) and is restated at the bottom by renderPlan. The defensible concern is verbosity / lack of a structured top-level next-action field for a pure-text response — not reachability of the instruction, which is surfaced up front.

findings.title: Four incompatible next-step shapes coexist with no single owner: nextCalls[] vs nextCall vs nextActions-prose vs Next:-markdown
findings.claim: The same concept ('what to call next') is delivered in four incompatible encodings depending on which handler ran: (A) `nextCalls[]` structured `{tool,args}` array (route-menu only), (B) `nextCall` copy-paste STRING (launch only), (C) `nextActions`/`nextStep`/`nextSteps` PROSE string with tool+args embedded in a sentence (deploy/import/env/subdomain/scale/manage/export/git-push-setup), (D) `Next:` markdown bullet inside a `_text` blob (develop/status prose). An agent cannot learn one parsing rule; it must branch on response-kind. This is a tell==check / single-owner violation at the delivery layer — there is no one owner of 'next action shape'.
findings.payload_evidence: route-menu nextCalls[] = `[{"tool":"zerops_workflow","args":{"action":"start","route":"recipe","recipeSlug":"nestjs-minimal",...}}]` (samples/workflow-bootstrap-discover-route-menu.json); launch nextCall = `"zerops_workflow action=\"start\" workflow=\"launch-production\" productionProjectName=\"api-prod\""` (samples/workflow-status-launch-active.json); deploy nextActions = `"Dev-mode dynamic runtime is idle… Start the dev server: zerops_dev_server action=start. Then run zerops_verify."` (samples/deploy.json).
findings.rendering_owner: (A) tools/workflow_bootstrap.go route-menu nextCalls; (B) tools/launch_status_recovery.go:74; (C) ops/deploy_common.go:25/72 `NextActions string` + tools/next_actions.go + tools/workflow_export.go:339; (D) internal/workflow/render.go:renderPlan.
findings.why_it_matters: RIGHT-INFO + REACHABILITY: the agent's most frequent decision (what to call next) has no uniform, machine-readable home. The route-menu/launch paths prove the structured form is achievable; the rest regressed to prose. Inconsistency forces per-kind parsing heuristics and produces nondeterministic agent behavior.
findings.proposed_direction: Adopt route-menu's `nextCalls[]{tool,args}` as the ONE canonical next-step shape across every response; the existing Plan.Primary already carries Tool+Args — serialize it, don't stringify it.

verdict.assessment:
All three verification axes check out against real evidence.

PAYLOAD QUOTES (all verbatim in plans/response-audit-corpus/samples/):
- workflow-bootstrap-discover-route-menu.json: nextCalls[] = structured [{"tool":"zerops_workflow","args":{"action":"start","route":"recipe","recipeSlug":"nestjs-minimal",...}}] — exact match.
- workflow-status-launch-active.json: nextCall = "zerops_workflow workflow=\"launch-production\" productionProjectName=\"api-prod\"" copy-paste STRING — exact match.
- deploy.json: nextActions = "Dev-mode dynamic runtime is idle (no start command). Start the dev server: zerops_dev_server action=start. Then run zerops_verify." PROSE string — exact match.
- workflow-develop-start-prose.json: "Next: zerops_deploy targetService=..." and "Next:\n  ▸ Primary: Deploy app — zerops_deploy targetService=\"app\"" markdown bullets inside a _text blob — exact match (shape D).

CODE OWNERS (each symbol produces the cited bytes):
- (A) bootstrap route-menu nextCalls[] — structured {tool,args}.
- (B) internal/tools/launch_status_recovery.go:74 — literally constructs NextCall = `zerops_workflow action="start" workflow="launch-production" productionProjectName="`+name+`"`. Field decl line 33.
- (C) internal/ops/deploy_common.go:25 `NextActions string` + internal/tools/next_actions.go:53 deploySuccessNextActions (produces the deploy.json string byte-for-byte) + internal/tools/workflow_export.go:339 nextSteps []string + internal/tools/workflow_git_push_setup.go + workflow_build_integration.go nextStep + ops/env.go,manage.go,subdomain.go,import.go nextActions + tools/scale.go:71.
- (D) internal/workflow/render.go:389 renderPlan ("Next:") + :245 blockerNextAction ("Next: zerops_deploy...").

DEFECT REAL, NOT MITIGATED: corpus-wide field-name census from index.jsonl top_keys: nextActions×1472, nextStep×194, nextCall×44, nextSteps×38, nextCalls×2 — plus the markdown Next: form (not a JSON key). That is SIX distinct JSON field names (claim said five — it folded nextStep singular into nextSteps) across THREE value encodings (structured {tool,args} array / copy-paste string / prose string-or-array) plus markdown-in-_text. The structured nextCalls form appears in only 2 of ~428 responses, proving the machine-readable form is achievable yet near-universally regressed to prose. No unifying owner exists: internal/workflow/compose.go (the R1 "presentation composer") is a byte-budget atom-demoter, not a next-action normalizer; the R2 single-owner lint (lint_accept_list_pin_test.go) pins something unrelated. deploy.json carries the prose nextActions as its ONLY machine-readable next-step. This is a genuine tell-shape single-owner violation at the delivery layer on the agent's most frequent decision.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED: (1) "a unifying composer already normalizes shape" — false, compose.go only demotes atoms under cap. (2) "prose nextActions also has a structured twin in the same response" — false, deploy.json has no nextCall/nextSteps alongside it. (3) "claim over-counts" — opposite, it under-counts (6 field names, not 5).

The claim slightly under-enumerates (nextStep singular vs nextSteps plural are distinct keys, both prose, different handlers), which strengthens the finding.
verdict.corrected_claim: The finding holds as stated, with one strengthening correction: the fan-out is SIX distinct JSON field names, not the implied five — `nextStep` (singular, git-push-setup + build-integration) is a separate key from `nextSteps` (plural array, export). Full inventory with corpus counts: nextCalls[] structured {tool,args} array (route-menu, ×2) | nextCall copy-paste string (launch, ×44) | nextActions prose string (deploy/import/env/subdomain/scale/manage, ×1472) | nextSteps[] array-of-prose-strings (export, ×38) | nextStep prose string (git-push-setup/build-integration, ×194) | Next: markdown bullet in _text blob (develop/status via render.go). Three value encodings plus markdown-in-text; no single owner; the structured form (nextCalls) is used in only 2 of ~428 responses.

findings.title: Mutation responses (deploy/import/env/subdomain) carry their next-call as a prose `nextActions` string, not an executable object
findings.claim: Every mutation handler models its post-action next-step as `NextActions string` (ops/deploy_common.go:25/72, ops/import.go:35, ops/env.go:27/42, ops/subdomain.go:115, ops/manage.go:36). The string embeds the tool name and args inside English prose. The agent must extract `zerops_dev_server action=start` + `zerops_verify` from a sentence rather than receive `[{tool:"zerops_dev_server",args:{action:"start"}},{tool:"zerops_verify",args:{}}]`. These are the highest-volume responses (deploy 474, import 280) so the prose-parse tax recurs constantly.
findings.payload_evidence: deploy.json (781B): `"nextActions":"Dev-mode dynamic runtime is idle (no start command). Start the dev server: zerops_dev_server action=start. Then run zerops_verify."`; import.json (825B): `"nextActions":"Verify services: zerops_discover. Continue workflow: mount dev, discover env vars, write code, then deploy."`
findings.rendering_owner: internal/ops/deploy_common.go:25,72 (`NextActions string`); literal prose at internal/tools/next_actions.go (nextActionImportSuccess etc.) + tools/deploy_poll.go:71 (deploySuccessNextActions).
findings.why_it_matters: STRUCTURED_PROSE: a tool name inside a sentence is not a callable. import.json even chains a multi-step plan ('mount dev, discover env vars, write code, then deploy') as one comma-list — five sequential actions with zero structure. The agent must sequence them by reading English.
findings.proposed_direction: Replace the `NextActions string` fields with `nextCalls []NextAction` (reuse workflow.NextAction); keep a human `message` for the operator, but the agent acts on the typed array.

verdict.assessment:
PAYLOAD: Both cited samples exist verbatim. plans/response-audit-corpus/samples/deploy.json (781B) carries the EXACT quoted nextActions string ("Dev-mode dynamic runtime is idle (no start command). Start the dev server: zerops_dev_server action=start. Then run zerops_verify."); import.json (825B) carries the exact "Verify services: zerops_discover. Continue workflow: mount dev, discover env vars, write code, then deploy." Sizes, bytes, and kind all match. Volume confirmed in stats.json: zerops_deploy=474, zerops_import=280 — the two highest-volume mutation tools.

CODE OWNER: All 6 cited NextActions field decls confirmed at exact lines — ops/deploy_common.go:25 (DeployResult) + :72 (GitPushResult), ops/import.go:35, ops/env.go:27+:42, ops/subdomain.go:115, ops/manage.go:36; every one is `NextActions string`. The literal-prose producers match byte-for-byte: internal/tools/next_actions.go:53 (deploySuccessNextActions deferred-start branch == deploy.json) and :18 (nextActionImportSuccess == import.json), wired via deploy_poll.go:71 (result.NextActions = deploySuccessNextActions(...)) and import.go:332 (result.NextActions = nextActionImportSuccess).

DEFECT REAL: On the success path the next-step is modeled SOLELY as a prose string. Grepped all 5 success result structs — zero structured next-call object (topology.Recovery / [{tool,args}]) on success; Recovery only exists on error/CheckResult paths. The agent must extract `zerops_dev_server action=start` from a sentence, and the import response genuinely chains five sequential steps as one comma-list with no structure. Adversarial mitigation check: deploy.json carries workSessionState.progress.pending=[appdev,appstage], but that is a session-scope tracker, not a next-tool-call — it does not name the next tool, so it does NOT mitigate. Claim is not stylistic-only: the gap is structural (string vs callable). However the prose is well-formed, non-contradictory, route-aware and single-owner-derived (not hand-drift, not buried) — a capable LLM parses it reliably — so the real harm is recurring parse-tax + unstructured multi-step chain, not ambiguity/error.
verdict.corrected_claim: Holds as stated, but the harm is a recurring prose-parse tax and an unstructured 5-step chain in the import case — NOT agent-blocking ambiguity. The strings are well-formed, non-contradictory, and (for deploy) route-aware single-owner-derived, so a competent agent extracts the tool+args reliably; the cost is parse overhead and the absence of a machine-executable [{tool,args}] form, not incorrect action.

findings.title: Export classify-prompt: the next action is a prose `nextSteps[]` and `fetchValuesVia` string under an 18KB guidance blob
findings.claim: `workflow:export:start::status=classify-prompt` is 23.8KB; 17.8KB of it is the `guidance` prose field. The actual next-action lives in `nextSteps` (a 2-element string array, awkwardly line-split) and `fetchValuesVia` (a prose command string) — neither is an executable `{tool,args}`. The agent must read 18KB to learn it should re-call export with `envClassifications={...}`, a fact that fits in a 2-field structured object.
findings.payload_evidence: workflow-export-start-status-classify-prompt.json, 23768 bytes, guidance=17839 bytes; `nextSteps`=[`"Re-call: zerops_workflow workflow=\"export\" targetService=\"appdev\""`, `"        envClassifications={key:bucket,...}"`]; `fetchValuesVia`=`"zerops_discover service=\"appdev\" includeEnvs=true includeEnvValues=true"`.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/tools/workflow_export.go:classifyPromptResponse (402) + renderExportStatusGuidance (270) → workflow.RenderExportGuidance; nextSteps assembled inline (workflow_export.go:339/371 pattern).
findings.why_it_matters: HOW-MUCH + REACHABILITY: 75% of the payload is reference prose; the decision-critical re-call shape is a fragmented string below it. The split across two array elements (the second is just leading-whitespace continuation) shows the prose form actively corrupts the instruction.
findings.proposed_direction: Surface the re-call as a structured `nextCall:{tool:"zerops_workflow", args:{workflow:"export", targetService:..., envClassifications:<table>}}`; keep the env table structured (it already is via envClassificationTable) and demote the 18KB intro to optional detail.

verdict.assessment:
PAYLOAD: Every quoted fact verified exactly against plans/response-audit-corpus/samples/workflow-export-start-status-classify-prompt.json (and index.jsonl). Total 23,768B wrapper / 23,629B inner; guidance=17,839B=75.5% of payload. nextSteps is exactly the 2-element string array with the awkward whitespace-continuation 2nd element ["Re-call: zerops_workflow workflow=\"export\" targetService=\"appdev\"", "        envClassifications={key:bucket,...}"]. fetchValuesVia is exactly the prose string "zerops_discover service=\"appdev\" includeEnvs=true includeEnvValues=true". No field anywhere is an executable {tool,args} object (all top-level fields are str / list-of-str / list-of-flat-dict).

CODE OWNER: Confirmed at internal/tools/workflow_export.go:classifyPromptResponse (line 402). fetchValuesVia assembled inline via fmt.Sprintf (line 438), nextSteps as inline []string{} (lines 439-442, line 441 IS the literal 8-space-leading continuation). guidance (line 437) = renderExportStatusGuidance (line 270) -> workflow.RenderExportGuidance (synthesize_export.go:98), which joins static atom bodies with "\n\n---\n\n". Matches cited owner precisely.

DEFECT REAL: guidance is a STATIC atom-corpus join (2 atoms), NOT live-derived — zero mentions of live hostname 'appdev' (uses literal {targetHostname} placeholder x2), zero mentions of live env keys GIT_TOKEN/ZCP_API_KEY. Same ~17.8KB re-emitted every classify-prompt. The guidance ALSO restates the full re-call (envClassifications= x7 in prose) — pure redundancy with the structured fields. 'Buried' confirmed structurally: Go marshals map keys alphabetically, so nextSteps serializes at byte offset 18,911, physically after the entire guidance blob (offset 615-18,911) — second-to-last field.

NARROWING (severity high->medium): the reachability framing slightly overstates harm. An MCP agent receives parsed JSON and can index nextSteps/fetchValuesVia/envClassificationTable directly without linearly scanning the 18KB; the keys+suggested-buckets are already in the top-of-object envClassificationTable (offset 1). So the next-action is REACHABLE without the prose — the real defect is HOW-MUCH (75% redundant static reference prose re-emitted every turn) plus a genuinely-corrupted instruction shape (whitespace-split nextSteps element + string-typed fetchValuesVia instead of an executable object), not a hard reachability block.
verdict.corrected_claim: The factual core holds verbatim: workflow:export:start::status=classify-prompt is 23.8KB with 17.8KB (75.5%) static, non-live-derived guidance prose, and the re-call shape lives in a string-typed nextSteps array (awkwardly split across two elements, the second being leading-whitespace continuation) + a prose fetchValuesVia string — neither an executable {tool,args}. nextSteps physically serializes at byte offset 18,911, after the entire guidance blob. The defect is primarily HOW-MUCH (75% redundant reference prose re-emitted every turn, duplicating the re-call the structured fields already carry) and instruction-shape quality, NOT a hard reachability block: an MCP agent indexes the structured top-level fields (envClassificationTable at offset 1, fetchValuesVia, nextSteps) directly without scanning the prose, so the next-action is reachable. Refine the dimension from REACHABILITY to HOW-MUCH and severity from high to medium.

findings.title: availableStacks (1.2KB prose stack table) re-dumped on 618 session-active responses — surface-once violation
findings.claim: The `availableStacks` field — a 1214-byte markdown table ('## Available Service Stacks (live, active concrete versions)…') — is re-emitted on EVERY bootstrap/recipe/adopt session-active response: 618 occurrences across the corpus. It is identical project-to-project within a session and irrelevant after the import-YAML step is authored. This is a textbook surface-once / recommend-don't-enumerate violation: the full validation-set (every stack) is presented as a per-turn choice menu the agent re-reads each step.
findings.payload_evidence: availableStacks present on 618 index.jsonl rows; component sizes in by-type.md: workflow:bootstrap/classic:start::session-active availableStacks=1214, bootstrap/adopt=1214, bootstrap/recipe=1214; sample text `"## Available Service Stacks (live, active concrete versions)\nPick a concrete version…"`.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/workflow/bootstrap.go:74 (`AvailableStacks string`), set at internal/tools/workflow_bootstrap.go:296; recipe.go:248.
findings.why_it_matters: REDUNDANCY: 1.2KB × 618 = ~750KB of repeated reference prose across sessions. Re-dumping the full stack enum every turn is exactly 'validation-set presented as choice-set' — the agent only needs it once (at plan-authoring), and only the curated correct picks, not the whole list re-shown at close-step.
findings.proposed_direction: Emit availableStacks ONCE on the plan-authoring step (provision/classic-start), not on every session-active turn; downstream steps reference it by having-seen-it, not re-include.

verdict.assessment: PAYLOAD: Confirmed — 618 index.jsonl rows carry availableStacks; the field is the verbatim "## Available Service Stacks (live, active concrete versions)\nPick a concrete version…" markdown (parsed from sample response_text: content len 1173, 1214 incl JSON key+quoting). by-type.md confirms size 1214 on bootstrap/classic|adopt|recipe:start::session-active. CODE OWNER: Confirmed — field at internal/workflow/bootstrap.go:74, set at internal/tools/workflow_bootstrap.go:296 (populateStacks), recipe.go:248. BUT the finding's LOAD-BEARING claim ("re-emitted on EVERY bootstrap/recipe/adopt session-active response… re-shown at close-step… re-read each step… surface-once violation") is REFUTED by the current code. Every populateStacks caller is guarded by needsStacks() (workflow_bootstrap.go:31-36), which returns true ONLY when resp.Current!=nil && Current.Name=="discover" (stackSteps={StepDiscover:true}). The doc-comment lines 25-30 describe the EXACT fix the finding proposes — "it re-shipped on every status/transition/completed response… Presentation is now one-shot at the decision point" — landed in commit 09078b84 (2026-06-03 "present active concrete versions, once at discover"). Pinned by TestWorkflowTool_BootstrapStatus_NoStacks_DeployStep + TestWorkflow_BootstrapComplete_IncludesStacks_OnDiscoverStep. CORPUS PROOF: the 618 rows span suites 2026-05-03→06-05 (mixes pre/post-fix). Splitting on the fix timestamp: PRE-fix (507 rows) DO leak onto complete:close (147), complete:provision (83), ?:complete::obj (18) — exactly the symptom the finding describes. POST-fix (111 rows) carry availableStacks ONLY on bootstrap/*:start::session-active (which land on the discover step — verified current.name='discover' in post-fix samples) plus 1 stray status; ZERO on close or provision. Post-fix close/provision samples have current.name='close'/None and availableStacks absent. So the 750KB/618×/surface-once redundancy is STALE: it measures a corpus dominated by pre-fix transcripts; the defect was already corrected before the audit ran. Residual: FormatStackList (internal/knowledge/versions_format.go:11) does emit the full active-version catalog (a validation-set-shaped list) AT the discover step — but it is already curated (strips family aliases + rolling tags, active-concrete-only, "pass another version if you want") and shown ONCE at the plan-authoring decision point, the correct time. Narrowing it further is legitimate but stylistic taste, not the high-severity wrong-time surface-once redundancy claimed.
verdict.corrected_claim: The surface-once/redundancy defect (availableStacks re-dumped on close/provision/status/completed responses) was REAL but is already fixed: commit 09078b84 (2026-06-03) gates the field to the discover step only via needsStacks(), pinned by TestWorkflowTool_BootstrapStatus_NoStacks_DeployStep. In the current code the 1173-byte catalog is emitted ONCE at the discover step (plan-authoring decision point), not re-shown at close-step. The corpus's 230 close/provision occurrences are all pre-fix; post-fix suites show zero. The only surviving (separate, low) observation is stylistic: FormatStackList still lists the full active-concrete catalog (already alias-/rolling-tag-stripped and curated) rather than a narrower recommend-don't-enumerate pick-set — but at the correct one-shot time.

findings.title: session-active current.detailedGuide is a 5.5KB prose blob shipped every step alongside a tools[] that names tools but carries no args
findings.claim: The session-active `current` dict carries `detailedGuide` (5.5KB prose) + `tools` (array of bare tool NAMES, no args/sequence) + `verification` (167B prose). The `tools[]` field is the structured skeleton of a next-step but is gutted: it lists `["zerops_discover","zerops_knowledge","zerops_workflow"]` — names only — while the actual how-to lives in the 5.5KB detailedGuide prose. So the response has a structured slot (tools[]) that COULD be executable but instead just names tools, and the real instruction is prose. Repeats per step.
findings.payload_evidence: workflow-bootstrap-classic-start-session-active.json: current.tools=`["zerops_discover","zerops_knowledge","zerops_workflow"]`; current.detailedGuide STRING len=5572; current.verification STRING len=167. By-type.md: workflow:complete:provision::session-active current=4326 avg bytes.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/workflow/bootstrap.go:162 (DetailedGuide), :301 (buildGuide); recipe.go:289/469.
findings.why_it_matters: STRUCTURED_PROSE + HOW-MUCH: `tools[]` is a half-built structured next-step — names without args means the agent still parses detailedGuide for the actual call. The structure exists but doesn't carry the load; the 5.5KB prose does.
findings.proposed_direction: Promote `tools[]` to `nextCalls[]{tool,args}` (the step already knows the expected call shape); keep detailedGuide as optional pull-on-ambiguity, not the primary instruction.

verdict.assessment:
VERIFIED against real payload + code owner; the finding holds.

(1) PAYLOAD — samples/workflow-bootstrap-classic-start-session-active.json. Parsing the embedded response_text: current.tools == ["zerops_discover","zerops_knowledge","zerops_workflow"] (exact match); len(current.detailedGuide)==5572 (claim said 5572, "5.5KB" rounding correct); len(current.verification)==167 (exact). by-type.md line 32 confirms workflow:complete:provision::session-active current=4326 avg bytes (exact). Walked the entire response object: the ONLY list fields are current.tools (bare names) and progress.steps (status tuples). There is NO structured next-call slot anywhere — no nextCall/args/parameters. The exact call the agent must emit (zerops_workflow action="complete" step="discover" + the plan JSON shape) exists ONLY as text inside the 5572B detailedGuide prose. So the structured slot (tools[]) names tools but carries no args/sequence, and the real instruction is prose — exactly as claimed.

(2) CODE OWNER — bootstrap.go:160-162 declares BootstrapStepInfo.{Tools []string, Verification string, DetailedGuide string}. bootstrap.go:296 sets Tools: detail.Tools (a STATIC []string from stepDetails in bootstrap_steps.go:17-33 — discover's Tools literal == the payload exactly), and :301 sets DetailedGuide = b.buildGuide(...). buildGuide lives in bootstrap_guide_assembly.go:23 (the finding cited bootstrap.go:301 for buildGuide — that is the CALL site, accurate; the func body is in the assembly file — minor citation imprecision, not a defect). buildGuide assembles atom bodies via Synthesize + strings.Join(BodiesOf(matches),"\n\n---\n\n") = a prose markdown blob. recipe.go:289/465/469 mirror the identical pattern (static Tools names + prose DetailedGuide via recipe_guidance.go:34 buildGuide). So the cited symbols genuinely PRODUCE these bytes, and the defect repeats per step across both bootstrap and recipe session-active families.

(3) DEFECT REAL? Structurally yes — tools[] is a half-built structured next-step (names without args), and the load-bearing instruction is unavoidably in prose because no structured call-slot exists in the response. NOT refuted as a structure-quality issue. The defect is genuine but its operational impairment is modest: the detailedGuide is markdown the LLM parses competently and DOES contain a copy-pasteable call line + a JSON plan example, and verification+message give a clear success criterion — the agent CAN act. This is a HOW_MUCH/structure-redundancy defect (a structured slot that doesn't carry its load), not a correctness blocker.

Narrowing only on impact framing (not on facts): the gutted tools[] forces the agent to read prose for the actual call, but the detailedGuide is competent markdown with a copy-pasteable call + JSON plan example, so this impairs response STRUCTURE/economy (a structured slot exists but doesn't carry the load) rather than blocking the agent's ability to act. Pattern is not unique to bootstrap-classic-start — it repeats for every bootstrap step (provision, close) and every recipe step (recipe.go same owner), so the "repeats per step" claim is broader than the single cited sample and is confirmed.

findings.title: Deploy's nextActions and subdomain claims are computed from stored mode/class, not re-read live, so the prose next-step can describe a stale runtime shape
findings.claim: deploySuccessNextActions (tools/next_actions.go) branches on `topology.IsDeferredStart(mode, class)` where mode/class come from the bootstrap-time ServiceMeta, not a live discover at deploy-send-time. The emitted prose ('Dev-mode dynamic runtime is idle… Start the dev server') is therefore derived from a stored snapshot of the service shape. If the service was rescaled/changed mode between bootstrap and this deploy, the prose next-step is a stale tell. Because it's prose (not a field the agent cross-checks against live discover), the staleness is invisible.

Start the dev server: zerops_dev_server action=start…"` — keyed on mode/class; deploy_poll.go:71 `result.NextActions = deploySuccessNextActions(result, mode, class)` where mode/class are passed in from meta, not re-derived from a send-time discover.
findings.rendering_owner: internal/tools/deploy_poll.go:71 + internal/tools/next_actions.go:deploySuccessNextActions; predicate topology.IsDeferredStart.
findings.why_it_matters: TIMING/LIVE-TRUTH: the next-step instruction is derived from a stored proxy of the service shape. A prose string gives the agent no field to reconcile against live state; a structured nextCall referencing the live-resolved class would at least be auditable. Lower severity because mode rarely flips mid-session, but the prose form hides any drift that does occur.
findings.proposed_direction: Derive the post-deploy next-step from the live deploy-result's resolved service shape (the API already returned targetServiceType in the same response) rather than passed-in meta; ship it structured so the agent can cross-check.

findings.title: route-menu proves the right model exists, but it ALSO re-dumps the full prose `message` reciting the same options it already structured
findings.claim: `workflow:bootstrap:discover::route-menu` is the one fully-correct structured model (nextCalls[]{tool,args}) — yet it ALSO carries a 1150-byte prose `message` field that re-recites every option in English ('Options:\n  1. route="recipe" recipeSlug="nestjs-minimal"…') AND the full importYaml for every routeOption (1563 bytes summed). So even the good model double-encodes: structured nextCalls[] + redundant prose message + N full import YAMLs the agent only needs for the ONE route it picks. This is enumerate-don't-recommend: all routes' full YAML shown, when only the chosen route's matters.

findings.rendering_owner: internal/tools/workflow_bootstrap.go (route-menu assembly: routeOptions + nextCalls + message).
findings.why_it_matters: RIGHT-INFO-RIGHT-TIME: presenting all N routes' full import YAML up front is the validation-set-as-choice-set anti-pattern. The agent picks one route then has consumed 3× the bytes. The prose `message` duplicates what nextCalls[] already encodes structurally.
findings.proposed_direction: Keep nextCalls[] as the actionable surface; drop the prose `message` recitation (redundant with structured options) and defer per-route importYaml to the moment a route is chosen (or summarize, don't dump all three).
